                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • S122
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A matching engine is the one design where the answer is a single-threaded, in-memory, deterministic process — and knowing that is the point of the question. Correctness under price-time priority requires a total order of events, and the cheapest total order is one thread.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Everything else scales around it: the network layer, risk checks, and market-data fan-out are all parallel and horizontal. The book itself is one sequenced stream, replicated by shipping the input log to replicas that replay it deterministically — not by replicating the resulting state.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Determinism is what makes recovery and audit possible: given the same ordered inputs, every replica reaches the same book. So the durability requirement is on the sequenced input log, and a restart is a replay, which is a very different design from a database-backed service.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                One thread, one log
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                THE BOOK
  bids: price levels descending | asks: price levels ascending
  each level: a FIFO queue of orders (time priority within price)
  -> an array of price levels + intrusive linked lists
  -> add / cancel / match are all O(1) at the touch

MATCHING  (price-time priority)
  incoming BUY at limit P:
    while best ask <= P and quantity remains:
       fill against the FRONT of that price level (earliest first)
       emit a TRADE for each fill
    any remainder RESTS on the book at P
  a MARKET order does the same with no price limit, and what does not
  fill is cancelled (or rejected, per venue rules)

WHY SINGLE THREADED
  the book is one shared structure with a strict total order.
  locking it from many threads costs more than one core's throughput,
  AND destroys determinism. One thread, pinned, no allocation in the
  hot path, no GC pauses -> millions of orders/sec is achievable.
  Scale by SHARDING BY INSTRUMENT, not by threading one book.

REPLICATION - ship the INPUT, not the state
  gateway -> SEQUENCER (assigns a global order) -> durable log
                                                -> primary engine
                                                -> replica engines
  every replica replays the same ordered log and reaches the same book.
  failover = promote a replica that has consumed the same offset.
  RECOVERY = replay the log from the last snapshot.

AROUND IT (all parallel, all horizontal)
  pre-trade risk checks, order validation, market-data fan-out,
  post-trade settlement, persistence of the trade record.

AUDIT: the sequenced log IS the audit trail. Regulators ask
"why did this trade happen at this price" and replay answers it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Follow-ups they will ask
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Why not shard the book across threads?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Because a single instrument's book is one ordered structure — splitting it breaks price-time priority, which is a correctness and regulatory property, not an optimisation. Sharding by instrument is fine and is how venues scale: each instrument gets its own single-threaded engine.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                What is the sequencer for?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                It assigns the single global order that makes everything downstream deterministic. Multiple gateways receive orders concurrently, but the sequencer decides what happened first, writes that to the durable log, and every engine and replica consumes the same sequence. It is the total-order primitive the whole design rests on.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • S123
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Statement history is write-once, read-recent, retain-forever — which is a different shape from most systems and should drive the design. The last 90 days get almost all the reads; seven years of history must exist but is queried rarely.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  So tier the storage: recent data in a hot partitioned store, older data rolled to cheap object storage in a columnar format, with a query layer that knows which tier to hit. Keeping seven years in the primary database is the expensive mistake.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Partition by (account_id, time) so a customer's statement is a single-partition range scan. Statement generation itself is an asynchronous job producing an immutable artifact — a PDF a customer downloads twice must be byte-identical, so generate once and store, never regenerate on demand.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Tiering and partitioning
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  ACCESS PATTERN - measure this, it drives everything
  ~95% of reads: last 90 days, one account, date range, newest first
  ~5%: older history, search by amount/merchant, regulatory export
  writes: append-only, never updated

PARTITIONING
  key (account_id, txn_time DESC)
  -> a statement query is ONE partition, ONE range scan, no fan-out
  -> beware the whale account: a corporate account with millions of
     transactions needs sub-partitioning by month

TIERING
  HOT    last 90d      partitioned OLTP store, indexed, low latency
  WARM   90d - 2y      same store, older partitions, cheaper hardware
                       or a separate analytics store
  COLD   2y - 7y       object storage, PARQUET, partitioned by
                       account-bucket/year/month; queried via a
                       query engine, seconds not milliseconds
  -> the API tells the user "older history may take a moment"
     and returns it asynchronously if needed

  rolling is a scheduled job: copy partition -> verify -> drop.
  VERIFY BEFORE DROP. Row counts and checksums.

STATEMENTS ARE IMMUTABLE ARTIFACTS
  generate ASYNC at period close -> render PDF -> store in object
  storage -> record the pointer + a checksum
  -> downloading twice gives the SAME BYTES. Regenerating on demand
     risks a different document for the same period, which is a
     compliance problem, not just a bug.

CORRECTIONS never edit history: a reversing entry appears in the
CURRENT period, referencing the original. The old statement stands.

RETENTION: 7 years is a legal floor, and deletion after it may be a
legal requirement too. Automate both ends.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Follow-ups they will ask
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  How do you support search across seven years?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Not from the transactional store. Index searchable fields into a separate search index covering the full range, with the object-storage records as the source of truth — the index returns pointers, and you fetch details from the appropriate tier. Accept higher latency for deep search and say so in the UI.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Why must a statement PDF be byte-identical on re-download?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Because it is a financial document a customer may have filed or submitted somewhere. If regeneration picks up a later correction or a template change, two copies of the same statement disagree, and there is no way to say which is authoritative. Generating once and storing the checksum makes the artifact the record.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • S124
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    KYC is a long-running, human-in-the-loop workflow — minutes to days, with external vendor calls and manual review. Model it as an explicit state machine persisted in a database, not as a chain of service calls; it is a saga where the compensations are mostly notifications and status reversals.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Every state transition is recorded with who or what caused it and when. That audit trail is a regulatory requirement, not a debugging convenience: a regulator asks why an account was approved, and the answer must be reconstructable years later.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Documents are sensitive personal data, which changes the storage design: encrypted at rest with a customer-scoped key, access logged on every read, retained on a legal schedule and then actually deleted. Storing an ID photo like an ordinary upload is the failure mode.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    An explicit state machine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    STATES  (persisted; every transition audited)
  INITIATED -> DOCS_UPLOADED -> AUTO_CHECKS -> {PASSED | REVIEW | FAILED}
  REVIEW -> (human) -> APPROVED | REJECTED | MORE_INFO_NEEDED
  MORE_INFO_NEEDED -> DOCS_UPLOADED   (loop)
  APPROVED -> PERIODIC_REREVIEW (risk-based, e.g. annually)

  transition record: from, to, actor (user | system | reviewer id),
                     reason, evidence refs, timestamp. IMMUTABLE.

AUTO CHECKS - several vendors, each unreliable
  document authenticity | face match to selfie | liveness
  sanctions & PEP screening | address verification | duplicate detection
  -> each is an async call with a timeout, retries, and a CIRCUIT BREAKER
  -> a vendor being down must NOT fail the application: park it in
     PENDING_VENDOR and resume. Orchestrated by a durable workflow
     (Temporal / a state machine + a scheduler), never an in-memory chain.

DOCUMENT STORAGE
  object storage, encrypted at rest, per-customer key
  access LOGGED on every read (who, when, why)
  signed short-lived URLs; never a public path
  retention schedule enforced by a job that ACTUALLY DELETES

REVIEW QUEUE
  prioritise by risk and by age; SLA per tier
  reviewers see redacted data by default, full data on justified access
  two-person approval above a risk threshold
  reviewer decisions become training data for the auto-checks

IDEMPOTENCY: vendor callbacks arrive twice. Key every transition on
(application_id, from_state, event) so a replay is a no-op.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Follow-ups they will ask
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Why a durable workflow engine rather than a chain of calls?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Because the process spans days and survives deploys, vendor outages and human delays. An in-memory orchestration loses its place on restart; a persisted state machine can be resumed, queried, timed out, and audited. It also makes where is my application answerable, which is most of the support load.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What happens when a vendor changes its answer?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Treat it as a new event on the existing application rather than a mutation — a sanctions list update can flip a previously-approved customer. That is why periodic re-review exists as a state: approval is a point-in-time decision, and the workflow must be able to re-enter review with the original decision still intact in the audit trail.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • S125
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The first decision is the isolation model, and it is mostly a business decision wearing a technical hat: shared database with a tenant column is cheapest and easiest to operate; database-per-tenant gives real isolation and a clean per-tenant restore; a hybrid puts large or regulated tenants on their own and pools the rest.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Whatever you choose, tenant isolation must be enforced structurally, not by remembering to add WHERE tenant_id = ?. A missed filter is a cross-tenant data leak, which is the one bug that ends a B2B product — so put it in the framework: row-level security, a session variable, or a data-access layer that cannot issue an unscoped query.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Then handle the noisy neighbour: per-tenant rate limits and quotas, so one tenant's bulk import does not degrade everyone. And make per-tenant the default dimension for every metric, because the system is fine and this customer's experience is fine are different claims.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Isolation, and the query you must not be able to write
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      ISOLATION MODELS
  SHARED DB, tenant_id column
    + cheapest, one schema to migrate, best density
    - leak risk is a code review away; noisy neighbours; no per-tenant
      restore; a huge tenant skews everything
  SCHEMA PER TENANT
    + logical separation, per-tenant backup is easier
    - migrations across thousands of schemas; connection pool pressure
  DATABASE PER TENANT
    + real isolation, per-tenant restore, per-tenant residency, easy
      "delete this customer"
    - cost and operational load scale with tenant COUNT
  HYBRID (the usual real answer)
    pooled by default; dedicated for enterprise, regulated, or noisy
    tenants. The MIGRATION PATH between them must exist from day one.

ENFORCING ISOLATION - structural, not disciplined
  Postgres RLS:
    ALTER TABLE invoice ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
    CREATE POLICY t ON invoice USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant')::uuid);
  set app.tenant per connection from the authenticated context.
  -> now a forgotten WHERE returns ZERO rows, not someone else's.
  and: tenant id comes from the TOKEN, never from a request parameter.

NOISY NEIGHBOURS
  per-tenant rate limits and quotas at the edge
  bulk/async work on a separate pool with per-tenant concurrency caps
  a slow query budget: kill it, do not let it hold a shared pool

PER-TENANT EVERYTHING
  metrics, logs, traces, and error budgets tagged with tenant id
  -> "p99 is fine" can hide one customer at 8 seconds
  billing usage is derived from these same events

MIGRATIONS at multi-tenant scale must be online and backward
compatible - you cannot take a maintenance window for one tenant.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Follow-ups they will ask
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      How do you onboard a new tenant?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      As an automated provisioning workflow, not a manual runbook — create the tenant record, seed defaults, apply the plan's quotas, and (in a dedicated model) provision and migrate the database. It should be a single idempotent operation that can be retried, because it will fail part-way at some point and half-created tenants are painful.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      How do you delete a tenant's data?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      In a database-per-tenant model it is dropping a database, which is why regulated customers are often put there. In a pooled model it is a coordinated delete across every table plus caches, search indexes, object storage, logs and backups — which is much harder to prove complete. If you have a contractual deletion obligation, let that shape the isolation model rather than discovering it later.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • L01
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Encapsulation is the only one that earns its keep on its own. It means the class owns its invariants — nobody outside can put it in an illegal state. A class with public setters for every field has the syntax of encapsulation and none of the benefit.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Abstraction is choosing what to hide. Inheritance is the most overused of the four and usually the wrong tool — see the next topic. Polymorphism is what actually pays: it is how you delete an if/else chain and how every behavioural pattern works.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The difference in practice
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        // Syntactically encapsulated, actually not
class Account {
    private double balance;
    public void setBalance(double b) { this.balance = b; }   // anyone, anything
    public double getBalance() { return balance; }
}

// Actually encapsulated - the class owns its invariant
class Account {
    private long balanceMinor;                    // no setter exists

    public void withdraw(long amount) {
        if (amount <= 0)               throw new IllegalArgumentException();
        if (amount > balanceMinor)     throw new InsufficientFunds();
        balanceMinor -= amount;                   // the ONLY way it decreases
    }
    public long balance() { return balanceMinor; }
}
// Now "balance can never go negative" is true by construction,
// not by every caller remembering to check.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Follow-ups they will ask
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        “Isn't a getter/setter pair the same as a public field?”
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Effectively yes, and that is the point. The value of a private field comes from not exposing a setter. If every field has both, you have written a struct with extra ceremony.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • L02
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Inheritance says is-a and inherits everything, including decisions you did not want. Composition says has-a and you forward only what you choose. The practical difference shows up when requirements combine: with inheritance, three independent variations need 2³ subclasses; with composition, three fields.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Use inheritance when there is a genuine substitutable is-a relationship and the base class was designed for extension. Use composition everywhere else, which is most places.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Subclass explosion vs composition
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          // INHERITANCE: every combination needs a class
class Coffee {}
class CoffeeWithMilk extends Coffee {}
class CoffeeWithSugar extends Coffee {}
class CoffeeWithMilkAndSugar extends Coffee {}      // 2^n and growing
class IcedCoffeeWithMilkAndSugarAndCream ...        // this is the smell

// COMPOSITION: combinations are runtime data
class Coffee {
    private final List<Addon> addons;
    Coffee(List<Addon> addons) { this.addons = List.copyOf(addons); }
    long price() {
        return addons.stream().mapToLong(Addon::price).sum() + BASE;
    }
}
new Coffee(List.of(MILK, SUGAR, CREAM));    // any combination, no new classes

// FRAGILE BASE CLASS - the reason inheritance bites
class Counter extends ArrayList<String> {
    int added = 0;
    public boolean add(String s)             { added++; return super.add(s); }
    public boolean addAll(Collection<String> c) { added += c.size(); return super.addAll(c); }
}
// If ArrayList.addAll internally calls add(), every element is counted TWICE.
// You cannot know that from the interface. That is the fragility.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Follow-ups they will ask
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          “When IS inheritance right?”
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          When the subclass is genuinely substitutable, the hierarchy is shallow and stable, and the base class was explicitly designed for extension — documented protected hooks, final on everything else. Template Method is the pattern that does this deliberately.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • L03
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Coupling is how many other classes you must understand or change to change this one. Cohesion is whether the members of a class serve one purpose. A class with high cohesion has a name that describes all of it, not a name plus 'and'.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            They trade off against each other at the extremes — one giant class has zero coupling and terrible cohesion; a thousand tiny classes have perfect cohesion and unmanageable coupling. The target is not maximum of either, it is the balance where a change stays local.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Reading the numbers off a class
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            // LOW cohesion - the name needs an "and"
class UserManager {
    void createUser(...)        {}
    void sendWelcomeEmail(...)  {}     // email concern
    void generateReport(...)    {}     // reporting concern
    void validateCreditCard(..) {}     // payments concern
}   // four reasons to change, four teams touching one file

// HIGH cohesion - each class has one job and one reason to change
class UserRepository  { void save(User u); Optional<User> byId(Id id); }
class WelcomeMailer   { void send(User u); }
class UserReport      { Report generate(DateRange r); }

// HIGH coupling - depends on a CONCRETE class and its internals
class OrderService {
    private MySqlOrderDb db = new MySqlOrderDb();      // cannot substitute
    void place(Order o) { db.connection().execute(...); }  // knows internals
}

// LOW coupling - depends on an abstraction it owns
class OrderService {
    private final OrderRepository repo;                // an interface
    OrderService(OrderRepository repo) { this.repo = repo; }
}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • L04
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The useful test is not counting methods, it is asking who requests changes. If the finance team asks for changes to the tax calculation and the ops team asks for changes to the report format, and both live in one class, that class has two reasons to change and two teams colliding in it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              SRP is the principle that produces the most classes, which is why people resist it. The payoff is that a change request maps to one file.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              One reason to change
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              // THREE reasons to change: business rules, storage, and presentation
class Employee {
    Money calculatePay()  { ... }     // changes when finance policy changes
    void  save()          { ... }     // changes when the database changes
    String toReportRow()  { ... }     // changes when reporting changes
}

// Split by WHO asks for the change
class Employee        { /* data + invariants only */ }
class PayCalculator   { Money calculate(Employee e); }   // finance owns this
class EmployeeRepo    { void save(Employee e); }         // platform owns this
class EmployeeReport  { String row(Employee e); }        // reporting owns this

// The test to apply out loud in an interview:
//   "Who would ask me to change this class?"
//   If the answer names two different people, split it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Follow-ups they will ask
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              “Doesn't this create too many tiny classes?”
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              It creates more classes and less code per change. The failure mode is real but rarer than the God class — apply SRP when you can name two distinct change requesters, not on every method.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • L05
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The signal is a conditional on a type or an enum that grows every time a feature is added. Each edit risks the cases you did not touch, and every edit needs the whole file re-reviewed and re-tested.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                OCP is not free: you pay in indirection and you must guess the right extension axis in advance. Guess wrong and you have an abstraction that fits nothing. The honest rule is to apply it on the second or third variation, not the first.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Adding a case without editing a file
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                // CLOSED to extension: every new shape edits this method
class AreaCalculator {
    double area(Shape s) {
        if (s instanceof Circle c)    return Math.PI * c.r * c.r;
        if (s instanceof Square sq)   return sq.side * sq.side;
        if (s instanceof Triangle t)  return 0.5 * t.b * t.h;
        throw new IllegalArgumentException();   // and this grows forever
    }
}

// OPEN: a new shape is a new class, and nothing existing is edited
interface Shape { double area(); }
record Circle(double r)   implements Shape { public double area(){ return Math.PI*r*r; } }
record Square(double s)   implements Shape { public double area(){ return s*s; } }
record Hexagon(double s)  implements Shape { public double area(){ ... } }  // NEW

// Strategy, State, Visitor and Chain of Responsibility all exist to
// deliver OCP along one particular axis.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Follow-ups they will ask
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                “When should I NOT apply OCP?”
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                On the first variation. An abstraction built for one case encodes a guess about what varies, and a wrong guess is more expensive than the if/else you avoided. Wait for the second or third case to show you the real axis.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • L06
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The classic example is Square extends Rectangle. Mathematically a square is a rectangle. In code, Rectangle promises that setting width leaves height alone — and Square cannot honour that. The inheritance is valid English and invalid design.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The practical test: can you replace the base with any subclass and have every existing test still pass? Preconditions may not be strengthened, postconditions may not be weakened, and invariants must be preserved.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The square/rectangle violation
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  class Rectangle {
    protected int w, h;
    void setWidth(int w)  { this.w = w; }
    void setHeight(int h) { this.h = h; }
    int area() { return w * h; }
}
class Square extends Rectangle {
    void setWidth(int w)  { this.w = w; this.h = w; }   // breaks the contract
    void setHeight(int h) { this.w = h; this.h = h; }
}

// Caller written against Rectangle - correct for every Rectangle:
void resize(Rectangle r) {
    r.setWidth(5);
    r.setHeight(4);
    assert r.area() == 20;      // FAILS for Square: area is 16
}
// Square is not substitutable. The fix is that neither should inherit
// from the other - both implement an immutable Shape.

// OTHER COMMON VIOLATIONS
class ReadOnlyList extends ArrayList {
    public boolean add(E e) { throw new UnsupportedOperationException(); }
}   // strengthens the precondition -> every caller must now know the subtype

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • L07
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Many small role-based interfaces beat one large one. The client should depend only on the methods it calls, so a change to an unrelated method does not force it to recompile or re-test.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The design heuristic: name interfaces after what the caller needs, not after the implementing class. Printable and Scannable, not MultiFunctionDevice.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Splitting by role
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    // FAT: every implementer must handle everything
interface Worker {
    void work();
    void eat();
    void attendStandup();
}
class RobotWorker implements Worker {
    public void work() { ... }
    public void eat() { throw new UnsupportedOperationException(); }  // smell
    public void attendStandup() { /* nothing */ }                     // smell
}

// SEGREGATED: implement only what applies
interface Workable  { void work(); }
interface Feedable  { void eat(); }
interface Attendee  { void attendStandup(); }

class HumanWorker implements Workable, Feedable, Attendee { ... }
class RobotWorker implements Workable { ... }               // honest

// Consumers narrow too - this method cannot accidentally eat()
void runShift(Workable w) { w.work(); }

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • L08
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The inversion is about which direction the source dependency points. Normally the business layer imports the database layer. With DIP, the business layer declares the interface it needs, and the database layer implements it — so the arrow now points inward, toward the domain.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      This is what makes the domain testable and swappable. It is also the foundation of hexagonal architecture, ports and adapters, and clean architecture — all three are DIP applied at module scale.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Who owns the interface
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      // NOT inverted: business logic imports infrastructure
package domain;
import infra.MySqlOrderDb;                    // domain -> infra   ✗
class OrderService {
    private MySqlOrderDb db = new MySqlOrderDb();
}

// INVERTED: the interface lives WITH the domain that needs it
package domain;
public interface OrderRepository {             // domain OWNS this
    void save(Order o);
    Optional<Order> byId(OrderId id);
}
public class OrderService {
    private final OrderRepository repo;        // depends on its own abstraction
    public OrderService(OrderRepository repo) { this.repo = repo; }
}

package infra;
import domain.OrderRepository;                 // infra -> domain   ✓
public class MySqlOrderRepository implements OrderRepository { ... }

// Both now depend on the abstraction. The domain compiles with no
// knowledge that a database exists - which is exactly the point.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Follow-ups they will ask
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      “Isn't this just an interface for the sake of it?”
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Only if the interface lives in the infrastructure package. Then it is ceremony. The value comes entirely from the domain declaring the interface, so the domain has no outward dependencies.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • L09
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        DRY is about knowledge, not text. Two identical code blocks that change for different reasons are not duplication — deduplicating them couples two things that should move independently, and the next requirement forces a boolean parameter into the shared function.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        KISS and YAGNI pull toward doing less. The rule of three is the usual practical compromise: duplicate freely twice, extract on the third occurrence, when you can finally see what actually varies.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        When DRY is wrong
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        // Two identical validations - but for DIFFERENT reasons
void validateSignupEmail(String e) {  if (!e.contains("@")) throw ...; }
void validateInvoiceEmail(String e) { if (!e.contains("@")) throw ...; }

// Tempting: extract to validateEmail(). Then six months later:
//   signup needs to reject disposable domains
//   invoicing must ACCEPT them (legacy customers)
// -> validateEmail(String e, boolean allowDisposable)
// -> and then a second flag, and a third. The abstraction is now worse
//    than the duplication was.

// THE TEST: "if requirement X changes, must BOTH copies change?"
//   yes -> same knowledge, extract it
//   no  -> coincidental duplication, leave it alone

// RULE OF THREE
//   1st: write it
//   2nd: duplicate it, note the similarity
//   3rd: now you can see what actually varies - extract THAT
