                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • L10
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Each dot past the first is a class whose structure you now depend on. The chain also tells you the responsibility is in the wrong place: instead of reaching in to compute something, ask the object that owns the data to compute it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The exception is fluent builders and streams, where the chain returns the same conceptual object rather than navigating a graph. Demeter is about navigation, not about dots.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Tell, don't ask
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          // VIOLATION: three classes coupled to read one field
String city = order.getCustomer().getAddress().getCity();
// Address changes shape -> this line breaks, and every line like it

// FIX 1: ask the nearest object
String city = order.customerCity();      // Order asks Customer, Customer asks Address

// FIX 2 (better): don't ask at all - TELL
// Instead of pulling data out to make a decision elsewhere:
if (order.getCustomer().getAccount().getBalance() > order.getTotal()) {
    order.getCustomer().getAccount().debit(order.getTotal());
}
// Move the decision to the object that owns the data:
customer.payFor(order);       // Customer knows its own account rules

// NOT a violation - a builder returns itself, it is not navigating
Order.builder().customer(c).item(i).quantity(2).build();

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • L11
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Information Expert is the one that does the most work: assign a responsibility to the class that has the data needed to fulfil it. Most misplaced methods are found by asking who already holds the information.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Creator says the class that contains or closely uses B should create B. Controller gives system events a single entry point. Low coupling and high cohesion are the tiebreakers when two placements both look reasonable.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Information Expert in action
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            // WRONG: the service computes from data it had to reach in for
class OrderService {
    Money total(Order o) {
        Money sum = Money.ZERO;
        for (LineItem li : o.getItems())            // reaching into Order
            sum = sum.plus(li.getPrice().times(li.getQty()));
        return sum;
    }
}

// INFORMATION EXPERT: the class holding the data does the work
class LineItem {
    Money subtotal() { return price.times(qty); }   // LineItem has price+qty
}
class Order {
    Money total() {                                 // Order has the items
        return items.stream().map(LineItem::subtotal)
                    .reduce(Money.ZERO, Money::plus);
    }
}

// THE GRASP QUESTION for any misplaced method:
//   "Which class already has the data this needs?"  -> put it there.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Saved links
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              1↗

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • L12
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Draw a class as a box with the name, then only the fields and methods that matter to the discussion. Never draw getters and setters. The relationships carry more information than the members do.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Say the cardinality out loud as you draw it — one parking lot has many floors, each floor has many spots, a spot holds zero or one vehicle. That sentence is the diagram.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The five arrows you need
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              ┌──────────────┐
│  ClassName   │
├──────────────┤
│ - field      │   -  private   + public   # protected
├──────────────┤
│ + method()   │
└──────────────┘

INHERITANCE      Child ──────▷ Parent          "is a"
IMPLEMENTS       Impl  ┄┄┄┄┄▷ Interface        "fulfils"
COMPOSITION      Whole ◆───── Part             "owns; dies with it"
                                                (Order ◆── LineItem)
AGGREGATION      Whole ◇───── Part             "has; outlives it"
                                                (Team ◇── Player)
ASSOCIATION      A ─────────> B                "uses / knows about"

CARDINALITY on the line, always:
   ParkingLot ◆──1───*── Floor ◆──1───*── Spot ──0..1──> Vehicle

// In a 45-minute round: boxes + relationships + cardinality.
// Skip visibility markers, skip method signatures, skip everything else.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Saved links
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                1↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                2↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                3↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • L13
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                An entity is the same thing over time even as its fields change — a User with a new email is still that user, because identity is the id. A value object has no id and is compared by value: two Money objects of ₹500 are interchangeable, and both should be immutable.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A service holds behaviour that does not belong to any single entity — usually because it coordinates several, or needs something external. Reach for a service only after checking that no entity is the information expert.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Three kinds of class
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                // ENTITY: identity survives change, mutable, equals() on id ONLY
class User {
    private final UserId id;              // identity
    private String email;                 // may change; still the same user
    @Override public boolean equals(Object o) {
        return o instanceof User u && id.equals(u.id);   // id, nothing else
    }
    @Override public int hashCode() { return id.hashCode(); }
}

// VALUE OBJECT: no id, immutable, equals() on ALL fields
record Money(long minor, Currency currency) {
    Money plus(Money o) {
        if (!currency.equals(o.currency)) throw new CurrencyMismatch();
        return new Money(minor + o.minor, currency);      // returns NEW
    }
}
record Address(String line1, String city, String pin) {}

// SERVICE: behaviour that belongs to no single entity
class TransferService {                    // touches two Accounts
    void transfer(Account from, Account to, Money amount) { ... }
}

// The test for a value object: would you mind if I swapped this instance
// for an identical one? If not, it is a value.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Saved links
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  1↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  2↗

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • L14
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The heuristic finds candidate classes, which is genuinely useful in the first two minutes. Where it fails is that not every noun deserves a class (some are attributes, some are value objects, some are the same concept named twice), and important classes are often not nouns in the statement at all — PricingStrategy, BookingPolicy, SpotAllocator.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  After the noun pass, do a second pass asking what varies. Every axis of variation is a candidate for an interface, and those are the classes that make the design extensible.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The two passes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  STATEMENT: "A parking lot has multiple floors. Each floor has spots of
different sizes. A vehicle is assigned the nearest available spot that
fits it. Pricing depends on vehicle type and duration."

PASS 1 - nouns (candidates)
  ParkingLot, Floor, Spot, Vehicle, Ticket, Payment
  -> discard: "size" is an attribute/enum, not a class
  -> merge:   "car"/"bike"/"truck" are one Vehicle hierarchy

PASS 2 - what VARIES  (this is the pass people skip)
  "nearest available spot that fits"   -> SpotAllocationStrategy
  "pricing depends on type + duration" -> PricingStrategy
  payment method                       -> PaymentProcessor
  These are NOT nouns in the statement, and they are the classes that
  make the design extensible.

PASS 3 - what does NOT vary
  Keep it concrete. An interface with one implementation and no second
  one on the horizon is ceremony, and interviewers notice.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • L15
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The mechanics are trivial — private constructor, static instance, static accessor. The judgment is knowing that it hides a dependency: a class using Logger.getInstance() has a dependency nothing in its signature reveals, so you cannot substitute it in a test.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Say this out loud in an interview: I'd use a singleton here, but I'd inject it rather than call getInstance(), so the dependency is visible and testable. That single sentence separates people who memorised the pattern from people who have maintained code using it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Three implementations, and the better answer
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    // 1. EAGER - simplest, thread-safe by classloading, no lazy benefit
class Config {
    private static final Config INSTANCE = new Config();
    private Config() {}
    public static Config getInstance() { return INSTANCE; }
}

// 2. HOLDER IDIOM - lazy AND thread-safe, no synchronization cost
class Config {
    private Config() {}
    private static class Holder { static final Config I = new Config(); }
    public static Config getInstance() { return Holder.I; }   // JVM guarantees it
}

// 3. ENUM - serialization- and reflection-safe (Effective Java's pick)
enum Config {
    INSTANCE;
    public void load() { ... }
}

// WHAT IS USUALLY BETTER: one instance, injected
class OrderService {
    private final Config config;
    OrderService(Config config) { this.config = config; }   // visible + swappable
}
// The container guarantees one instance. You keep the singleton
// LIFECYCLE without the global access point.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Follow-ups they will ask
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    “Why is Singleton called an anti-pattern?”
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Three reasons: it hides dependencies (nothing in the signature says you use it), it makes tests order-dependent because state persists between them, and it is a bottleneck under concurrency. The lifecycle is fine; the global static accessor is the problem.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Saved links
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      1↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      2↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      3↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • L16
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      new Config() is not atomic: allocate, construct, assign. The JVM may reorder the assignment before the construction finishes, so a second thread checking instance != null sees a reference to an object whose fields are still default values.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      volatile forbids that reordering and establishes the happens-before edge. In practice, prefer the holder idiom or an enum — both are correct with no synchronisation and less to get wrong.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Getting it right
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      // BROKEN - the classic wrong answer
class Config {
    private static Config instance;                    // NOT volatile
    static Config get() {
        if (instance == null) {
            synchronized (Config.class) {
                if (instance == null) instance = new Config();
            }
        }
        return instance;     // another thread can see a half-built object
    }
}

// CORRECT double-checked locking
class Config {
    private static volatile Config instance;           // volatile is REQUIRED
    static Config get() {
        Config local = instance;                       // one volatile read
        if (local == null) {
            synchronized (Config.class) {
                local = instance;
                if (local == null) instance = local = new Config();
            }
        }
        return local;
    }
}

// PREFERRED - correct with zero synchronization
class Config {
    private static class Holder { static final Config I = new Config(); }
    static Config get() { return Holder.I; }
}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • L17
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The pattern combines Template Method with construction. The base class owns the workflow and cannot know which product it needs; the subclass supplies it. That is why the creator is often abstract rather than a static utility.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        If you have a static method with a switch on a string, that is a simple factory — useful, but not Factory Method, and knowing the difference is a common interview probe.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Subclass decides the product
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        abstract class Dialog {
    // the algorithm lives here and does not change
    void render() {
        Button ok = createButton();          // <- the factory method
        ok.onClick(this::close);
        ok.draw();
    }
    protected abstract Button createButton();   // subclass decides
}

class WindowsDialog extends Dialog {
    protected Button createButton() { return new WindowsButton(); }
}
class WebDialog extends Dialog {
    protected Button createButton() { return new HtmlButton(); }
}

// Adding a platform = adding a subclass. Dialog.render() never changes.

// CONTRAST - simple factory, NOT the pattern (but often the right code):
class ButtonFactory {
    static Button create(String kind) {
        return switch (kind) {
            case "windows" -> new WindowsButton();
            case "web"     -> new HtmlButton();
            default        -> throw new IllegalArgumentException(kind);
        };
    }
}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Saved links
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          1↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          2↗

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • L18
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Simple Factory is a static method with a switch. It is not a pattern in the book, and it is frequently the right code — it centralises construction and that is often all you need.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Factory Method uses inheritance: a base class calls an abstract creator that subclasses override. Abstract Factory uses composition: you hold a factory object that produces a whole family of related products.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The three, side by side
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          // 1. SIMPLE FACTORY - not a GoF pattern. Often the right answer.
class ShapeFactory {
    static Shape create(String kind) {
        return switch (kind) {
            case "circle" -> new Circle();
            case "square" -> new Square();
            default -> throw new IllegalArgumentException(kind);
        };
    }
}
// + one place to change construction
// - adding a type edits this method (violates OCP)

// 2. FACTORY METHOD - INHERITANCE. Subclass decides ONE product.
abstract class Dialog {
    void render() { createButton().draw(); }      // algorithm fixed here
    protected abstract Button createButton();     // subclass supplies it
}
class WebDialog extends Dialog {
    protected Button createButton() { return new HtmlButton(); }
}

// 3. ABSTRACT FACTORY - COMPOSITION. One object makes a FAMILY.
interface GuiFactory {
    Button createButton();
    Checkbox createCheckbox();                    // family members that
}                                                 // MUST match each other
class Application {
    private final GuiFactory factory;             // held, not inherited
}

THE ANSWER TO GIVE
  Simple Factory   a static switch. Not a pattern. Fine most of the time.
  Factory Method   INHERITANCE, ONE product, subclass overrides.
  Abstract Factory COMPOSITION, a FAMILY, products must be compatible.

// If nothing forces the products to match, you do not need Abstract Factory.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Saved links
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            1↗

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • L19
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Factory Method makes one product; Abstract Factory makes a family, and its value is the guarantee that everything you get from one factory is compatible. That constraint is the whole justification for the extra interface.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The cost is rigidity: adding a new product type to the family means editing the factory interface and every implementation. Adding a new family is cheap. Know which direction your requirements grow before choosing it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            A family that must match
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            interface GuiFactory {                       // the family contract
    Button   createButton();
    Checkbox createCheckbox();
    Menu     createMenu();
}

class WindowsFactory implements GuiFactory {
    public Button   createButton()   { return new WindowsButton(); }
    public Checkbox createCheckbox() { return new WindowsCheckbox(); }
    public Menu     createMenu()     { return new WindowsMenu(); }
}
class MacFactory implements GuiFactory { /* all Mac widgets */ }

class Application {
    private final GuiFactory factory;
    Application(GuiFactory factory) { this.factory = factory; }
    void build() {
        Button b   = factory.createButton();     // guaranteed to match
        Checkbox c = factory.createCheckbox();   // the same OS family
    }
}

// THE TRADE-OFF
//   new FAMILY  (add Linux)        -> one new class          ✓ cheap
//   new PRODUCT (add Slider)       -> edit the interface AND
//                                     every implementation   ✗ expensive
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Follow-ups they will ask
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            “Factory Method vs Abstract Factory?”
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Factory Method creates one product and uses inheritance — subclasses override the creator. Abstract Factory creates a family and uses composition — you hold a factory object. If nothing forces the products to match, you do not need Abstract Factory.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Saved links
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              1↗

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • L20
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              It also solves readability — new Pizza(12, true, false, true) is unreadable at the call site, while .size(12).cheese().noOlives() is self-documenting. And it gives you one place to validate the whole object, at build(), rather than scattering checks.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Use it when there are roughly four or more parameters, several optional, or when the object should be immutable but has many fields.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Builder for an immutable object
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              public final class Pizza {
    private final Size size;             // required
    private final boolean cheese, pepperoni;
    private final List<String> toppings;

    private Pizza(Builder b) {           // private - only the builder constructs
        this.size = b.size; this.cheese = b.cheese;
        this.pepperoni = b.pepperoni;
        this.toppings = List.copyOf(b.toppings);   // defensive copy
    }

    public static Builder builder(Size size) { return new Builder(size); }

    public static final class Builder {
        private final Size size;                   // required -> constructor
        private boolean cheese, pepperoni;
        private final List<String> toppings = new ArrayList<>();

        private Builder(Size size) { this.size = Objects.requireNonNull(size); }
        public Builder cheese()              { this.cheese = true; return this; }
        public Builder topping(String t)     { toppings.add(t);    return this; }

        public Pizza build() {
            if (toppings.size() > 8) throw new IllegalStateException("too many");
            return new Pizza(this);       // ONE place to validate the whole object
        }
    }
}

Pizza p = Pizza.builder(LARGE).cheese().topping("basil").build();
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Saved links
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                1↗

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • L21
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Validate in build(), not in each setter. A half-built builder is allowed to be invalid; the constructed object never is. That is the invariant that makes the pattern worth the boilerplate.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Two refinements worth knowing: a toBuilder() method for creating a modified copy of an immutable object, and required parameters going in the builder's constructor rather than as optional setters — so the compiler enforces them.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Validation and copies
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                public Pizza build() {
    // cross-field rules that no single setter could check
    if (size == SMALL && toppings.size() > 3)
        throw new IllegalStateException("small pizza: max 3 toppings");
    if (vegan && cheese)
        throw new IllegalStateException("vegan pizza cannot have cheese");
    return new Pizza(this);
}

// Modifying an immutable object = copy with changes
public Builder toBuilder() {
    Builder b = new Builder(size);
    b.cheese = this.cheese;
    b.toppings.addAll(this.toppings);
    return b;
}
Pizza bigger = p.toBuilder().topping("olive").build();   // p is untouched

// Required params in the builder's constructor -> compiler-enforced
Pizza.builder(LARGE)        // cannot omit size; it will not compile
     .cheese().build();

// Java records give you immutability free, but no optional-parameter
// story - a compact canonical constructor plus a builder is common.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • L22
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The entire difficulty is shallow versus deep copy. A shallow copy shares mutable sub-objects with the original, so mutating the clone corrupts the source — a bug that appears far from its cause.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In Java, avoid Cloneable: it is widely regarded as broken (a protected method on Object, no constructor called, shallow by default). Prefer a copy constructor or an explicit copy() method you control.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Shallow vs deep, done explicitly
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  // AVOID Cloneable - shallow, no constructor runs, awkward contract
class Doc implements Cloneable {
    List<String> tags = new ArrayList<>();
    public Doc clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
        return (Doc) super.clone();       // SHARES the tags list. Bug.
    }
}
Doc b = a.clone();
b.tags.add("x");           // a.tags now also contains "x"

// PREFER a copy constructor - explicit, and it runs real construction
class Doc {
    private final String title;
    private final List<String> tags;
    private final Settings settings;      // mutable sub-object

    Doc(Doc other) {                                   // deep where it matters
        this.title    = other.title;                   // String: immutable, share
        this.tags     = new ArrayList<>(other.tags);   // copy the list
        this.settings = new Settings(other.settings);  // recursive deep copy
    }
    public Doc copy() { return new Doc(this); }
}

// RULE: immutable fields may be shared. Mutable fields must be copied,
// recursively, all the way down.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • L23
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Pooling pays when creation is genuinely expensive and objects are interchangeable — database connections, threads, large buffers. It does not pay for ordinary objects: modern allocators are fast, and a pool of cheap objects is slower than allocating, plus it defeats generational garbage collection.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The three things to get right are resetting state on return (or the next borrower sees the last one's data), enforcing a maximum with a timeout rather than unbounded growth, and detecting leaks when an object is never returned.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A pool that resets and bounds
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    class ConnectionPool {
    private final BlockingQueue<Connection> idle;
    private final Semaphore permits;                 // caps TOTAL, not just idle

    ConnectionPool(int max) {
        this.idle = new ArrayBlockingQueue<>(max);
        this.permits = new Semaphore(max);
    }

    Connection borrow(Duration timeout) throws InterruptedException {
        if (!permits.tryAcquire(timeout.toMillis(), MILLISECONDS))
            throw new PoolExhausted();               // bounded wait, not forever
        Connection c = idle.poll();
        return c != null ? c : create();
    }

    void release(Connection c) {
        c.reset();                       // CRITICAL: clear transaction state,
                                         // session vars, temp tables
        if (!c.isValid()) { c.close(); permits.release(); return; }
        idle.offer(c);
        permits.release();
    }
}

// THE CLASSIC BUG: using a connection after release().
// The next borrower gets the same object and you have two owners.
// try-with-resources on a wrapper is the usual defence.
