                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • L75
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The queue handles all coordination: put blocks when full, take blocks when empty. That covers backpressure and idle waiting with no wait/notify of your own.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The two things you must still get right are a bounded capacity and a clean shutdown. Interrupt handling in the consumer loop is where most implementations are subtly wrong.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The skeleton, end to end
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            // BOUNDED - always. An unbounded queue turns a throughput problem
// into an OutOfMemoryError.
BlockingQueue<Task> queue = new ArrayBlockingQueue<>(1000);

// THE API, and what each call does when it cannot proceed
queue.put(t);                     // BLOCKS until space      <- backpressure
queue.offer(t);                   // returns false immediately
queue.offer(t, 5, SECONDS);       // bounded wait, then false <- load shedding
queue.take();                     // BLOCKS until an item arrives
queue.poll(1, SECONDS);           // bounded wait, then null

// CONSUMER LOOP - the interrupt handling is what people get wrong
class Consumer implements Runnable {
    public void run() {
        while (!Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted()) {
            Task t;
            try {
                t = queue.take();
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();   // RESTORE the flag
                return;                               // and EXIT the loop
            }
            try {
                process(t);
            } catch (RuntimeException e) {
                log.error("task failed", e);          // do NOT let one bad
            }                                         // task kill the thread
        }
    }
}

// CLEAN SHUTDOWN - the poison pill
private static final Task STOP = new Task();

void shutdown(int consumerCount) throws InterruptedException {
    for (int i = 0; i < consumerCount; i++) queue.put(STOP);
}
// each consumer sees STOP and exits; no interrupt needed, and any
// work already queued still gets processed first

// CHOOSING THE IMPLEMENTATION
//   ArrayBlockingQueue     bounded, one lock          <- your default
//   LinkedBlockingQueue    UNBOUNDED by default - pass a capacity
//   SynchronousQueue       capacity 0: a direct handoff
//   PriorityBlockingQueue  ordered, unbounded
//   DelayQueue             items become available at a scheduled time
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            My notes

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • L76
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Sizing depends on the workload. CPU-bound work wants roughly the core count; I/O-bound work wants more, because threads spend most of their time blocked. The formula is cores × (1 + wait time / service time).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Always construct the executor explicitly rather than using the Executors factories, so the queue bound and the rejection policy are decisions you made rather than defaults you inherited.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Build it explicitly
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              // THE DEFAULT THAT KILLS SERVICES
ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(10);
// -> LinkedBlockingQueue with NO BOUND. Tasks queue until OutOfMemoryError.

// EXPLICIT - every choice visible
ThreadPoolExecutor pool = new ThreadPoolExecutor(
    10, 10,                                  // core, max
    60L, TimeUnit.SECONDS,                   // idle keep-alive
    new ArrayBlockingQueue<>(1000),          // BOUNDED
    new ThreadFactoryBuilder().setNameFormat("order-%d").build(),  // named!
    new ThreadPoolExecutor.CallerRunsPolicy() // backpressure: the submitter
);                                            // runs it, so it slows down

// REJECTION POLICIES
//   AbortPolicy         throws (default)
//   CallerRunsPolicy    submitter executes it -> natural backpressure
//   DiscardPolicy       drops silently  (rarely acceptable)
//   DiscardOldestPolicy drops the oldest queued task

// SIZING
//   CPU-bound: threads ≈ cores          (more just adds context switching)
//   I/O-bound: threads ≈ cores × (1 + waitTime/serviceTime)
//              e.g. 8 cores, 100ms wait, 10ms service -> 8 × 11 = 88

// ALWAYS name your threads. An unnamed pool-2-thread-7 in a stack trace
// tells you nothing at 3am.

// Java 21: virtual threads change the I/O-bound calculus entirely.
Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor();

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • L77
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                new Config() is three steps: allocate, construct, assign the reference. The JVM is permitted to reorder the assignment before construction finishes, so a second thread can see a non-null reference to an object whose fields are still zero.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                volatile forbids that reordering and establishes the happens-before edge. Knowing why it is needed — not just that it is — is what the question is testing.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Why volatile is not optional
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                // BROKEN - the answer most candidates give
class Config {
    private static Config instance;                    // NOT volatile
    static Config get() {
        if (instance == null) {                        // 1st check, no lock
            synchronized (Config.class) {
                if (instance == null)                  // 2nd check, locked
                    instance = new Config();
            }
        }
        return instance;
    }
}

// WHY IT IS BROKEN
//   instance = new Config()  is really three operations:
//     1. allocate memory
//     2. run the constructor
//     3. assign the reference to `instance`
//   The JVM may reorder 2 and 3. Thread B then sees instance != null
//   at the FIRST check, skips the lock entirely, and uses an object
//   whose fields are still default values.
//   This reproduces roughly never in testing and reliably in production.

// CORRECT
class Config {
    private static volatile Config instance;           // REQUIRED
    static Config get() {
        Config local = instance;                       // one volatile read
        if (local == null) {
            synchronized (Config.class) {
                local = instance;
                if (local == null) instance = local = new Config();
            }
        }
        return local;              // the local var avoids a second
    }                              // volatile read on the hot path
}

// PREFERRED - correct, lazy, and no synchronization at all
class Config {
    private Config() {}
    private static class Holder { static final Config I = new Config(); }
    static Config get() { return Holder.I; }
    // The JVM guarantees a class is initialised once, lazily, thread-safely.
}

// SAY THIS: "I'd use the holder idiom. But if you want double-checked
// locking, the field must be volatile, because otherwise another thread
// can see a partially constructed object."''

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • L78
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The classic case is transferring between two accounts: one thread locks A then B, another locks B then A. Sorting by a stable identity before locking makes both take them in the same order.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The alternatives are weaker: tryLock with a timeout turns deadlock into a retryable failure but does not prevent it, and detection after the fact means you already stalled.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Order the locks
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  // DEADLOCK: two threads, opposite order
void transfer(Account from, Account to, long amount) {
    synchronized (from) {
        synchronized (to) { ... }
    }
}
// transfer(A, B) and transfer(B, A) concurrently -> both wait forever

// FIX 1: GLOBAL ORDERING - the reliable one
void transfer(Account from, Account to, long amount) {
    Account first  = from.id() < to.id() ? from : to;    // stable order
    Account second = from.id() < to.id() ? to   : from;
    synchronized (first) {
        synchronized (second) {
            from.debit(amount); to.credit(amount);
        }
    }
    // Every thread now locks the lower id first. No cycle is possible.
}

// FIX 2: tryLock with timeout - degrades instead of hanging
if (from.lock.tryLock(1, SECONDS)) {
    try {
        if (to.lock.tryLock(1, SECONDS)) { ... }
        else return false;                       // back off and retry
    } finally { from.lock.unlock(); }
}

// DESIGN-LEVEL PREVENTION (best of all)
//   hold one lock at a time
//   never call unknown code (a listener, a callback) while holding a lock
//   never do I/O inside a lock
//   use an ordered aggregate: lock the Transfer, not both Accounts

// DIAGNOSING: jstack finds Java-level deadlocks automatically.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • L79
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The mechanism is a key the caller generates once per logical operation. The server records the key with its result, so a repeat returns the original outcome instead of performing the work again.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The subtlety is that recording the key and doing the work must be atomic. If they are not, a crash between them means the retry either duplicates the work or is wrongly rejected.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    An operation that can be repeated
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    // NOT idempotent - a retry charges twice
void charge(CardToken token, Money amount) {
    gateway.charge(token, amount);
}

// IDEMPOTENT - the caller supplies a key, once, per logical operation
@Transactional                                  // key + work in ONE transaction
PaymentResult charge(IdempotencyKey key, CardToken token, Money amount) {

    var existing = payments.byIdempotencyKey(key);
    if (existing.isPresent()) return existing.get().result();   // replay

    var result = gateway.charge(token, amount);
    payments.save(new Payment(key, result));    // atomic with the check
    return result;
}

// The unique constraint is what actually enforces it under concurrency:
//   CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON payments (idempotency_key);
// Two simultaneous retries: one inserts, the other gets a violation
// and re-reads the winner's result.

// NATURALLY IDEMPOTENT DESIGNS
//   SET status = 'paid'          (absolute)  ✓
//   balance = balance - 100      (relative)  ✗ not repeatable
//   INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING        ✓
//   DELETE WHERE id = 5                      ✓ (already gone is fine)

// KEY SCOPE: per logical operation, not per retry. The client generates
// it once and reuses it for every attempt - that is the entire point.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • L80
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Model the physical structure — lot, floor, spot, vehicle, ticket — then find the one axis that varies and make it an interface. That axis is spot allocation, and sometimes pricing.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The concurrency question is what separates a good answer: two cars arriving at once must not be assigned the same spot. Say how you handle it before being asked.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The core design
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      enum VehicleSize { MOTORCYCLE, COMPACT, LARGE }

record Vehicle(String plate, VehicleSize size) {}

class Spot {
    private final String id;
    private final VehicleSize size;
    private Vehicle occupant;                    // null = free

    boolean canFit(Vehicle v) { return occupant == null && size.ordinal() >= v.size().ordinal(); }
    synchronized boolean tryPark(Vehicle v) {    // ATOMIC test-and-set
        if (!canFit(v)) return false;
        occupant = v; return true;
    }
    synchronized Vehicle release() { var v = occupant; occupant = null; return v; }
}

class Floor { private final List<Spot> spots; }

// THE AXIS THAT VARIES -> Strategy
interface SpotAllocationStrategy { Optional<Spot> allocate(List<Floor> floors, Vehicle v); }
class NearestFirst  implements SpotAllocationStrategy { ... }
class LowestFloor   implements SpotAllocationStrategy { ... }

interface PricingStrategy { Money price(Duration d, VehicleSize s); }

class ParkingLot {
    private final List<Floor> floors;
    private final SpotAllocationStrategy allocator;
    private final PricingStrategy pricing;

    Ticket park(Vehicle v) {
        return allocator.allocate(floors, v)
            .filter(s -> s.tryPark(v))           // CAS: the race is here
            .map(s -> new Ticket(v, s, Instant.now()))
            .orElseThrow(LotFull::new);
    }
    Money unpark(Ticket t) {
        t.spot().release();
        return pricing.price(Duration.between(t.entryTime(), Instant.now()), t.vehicle().size());
    }
}

// SAY THIS OUT LOUD: "Two cars can be allocated the same spot, so
// tryPark is the atomic test-and-set. In a distributed version this
// becomes a conditional UPDATE with a WHERE occupant IS NULL."

// OVER-ENGINEERING TO AVOID: AbstractSpotFactory, VehicleVisitor,
// an event bus, a full observer chain. None of it is asked for.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • L81
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Model the elevator as a state machine (idle, moving up, moving down, doors open) with a set of pending requests. The scheduler decides which elevator serves a request and in what order.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Naming the SCAN/elevator algorithm — serve everything in the current direction, then reverse — shows you know the real answer rather than inventing nearest-first on the spot.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        State machine plus scheduler
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        enum Direction { UP, DOWN, IDLE }

class Elevator {
    private final int id;
    private int currentFloor;
    private Direction direction = Direction.IDLE;
    private final TreeSet<Integer> up   = new TreeSet<>();          // sorted
    private final TreeSet<Integer> down = new TreeSet<>(reverseOrder());

    void addStop(int floor) {
        if (floor > currentFloor) up.add(floor); else down.add(floor);
    }

    void step() {                       // SCAN: finish this direction first
        if (direction == Direction.UP) {
            var next = up.higher(currentFloor);
            if (next != null) { moveTo(next); return; }
            direction = down.isEmpty() ? Direction.IDLE : Direction.DOWN;
        }
        // symmetric for DOWN
    }
}

// THE AXIS THAT VARIES -> which elevator serves an external request
interface ElevatorScheduler {
    Elevator select(List<Elevator> bank, int floor, Direction wanted);
}
class NearestElevator implements ElevatorScheduler { ... }
class LeastBusy       implements ElevatorScheduler { ... }
class SameDirection   implements ElevatorScheduler {   // the good one
    // prefer an elevator already moving toward the floor, in the right direction
}

class ElevatorSystem {
    private final List<Elevator> bank;
    private final ElevatorScheduler scheduler;

    void requestFromFloor(int floor, Direction dir) {      // external button
        scheduler.select(bank, floor, dir).addStop(floor);
    }
    void requestInsideCar(int elevatorId, int floor) {     // internal button
        bank.get(elevatorId).addStop(floor);
    }
}

// SAY: "Internal and external requests are different - an internal
// request must go to THAT car; an external one can go to any."
// That distinction is what interviewers are listening for.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • L82
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          States: idle, item selected, money inserted, dispensing, out of stock. Each defines only the transitions legal from it, and everything else inherits a default that throws.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The details that show care: change calculation when exact change is unavailable, refunding on cancel, and what happens if dispensing fails halfway.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          State done properly
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          interface VendingState {
    default VendingState selectItem(String code) { throw new IllegalOp("select"); }
    default VendingState insertCoin(Coin c)      { throw new IllegalOp("insert"); }
    default VendingState dispense()              { throw new IllegalOp("dispense"); }
    default VendingState cancel()                { throw new IllegalOp("cancel"); }
}

class Idle implements VendingState {
    private final Machine m;
    public VendingState selectItem(String code) {
        Item item = m.inventory().get(code);
        if (item == null || item.stock() == 0) return new OutOfStock(m, code);
        return new AwaitingPayment(m, item);       // only legal move
    }
}

class AwaitingPayment implements VendingState {
    private final Item item; private Money inserted = Money.ZERO;

    public VendingState insertCoin(Coin c) {
        inserted = inserted.plus(c.value());
        return inserted.isAtLeast(item.price()) ? new ReadyToDispense(m, item, inserted)
                                                : this;      // stay
    }
    public VendingState cancel() { m.refund(inserted); return new Idle(m); }
}

class ReadyToDispense implements VendingState {
    public VendingState dispense() {
        Money change = inserted.minus(item.price());
        if (!m.canMakeChange(change)) {              // the detail people miss
            m.refund(inserted);
            return new Idle(m);
        }
        m.dispenseItem(item);
        m.dispenseChange(change);
        return new Idle(m);
    }
}

class Machine {
    private VendingState state = new Idle(this);
    public void selectItem(String code) { state = state.selectItem(code); }
    public void insertCoin(Coin c)      { state = state.insertCoin(c); }
    // no branching anywhere - the state objects ARE the diagram
}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • L83
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Same State structure — card inserted, PIN entered, transaction selected, dispensing. The difference is that debiting the account and dispensing cash must not diverge: money out with no debit, or a debit with no money out, are both unacceptable.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The cash dispensing algorithm itself is a small greedy or DP problem: make the amount from available denominations, and refuse cleanly if you cannot.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Transactions and denominations
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            interface AtmState {
    default AtmState insertCard(Card c) { throw new IllegalOp(); }
    default AtmState enterPin(String p) { throw new IllegalOp(); }
    default AtmState withdraw(Money m)  { throw new IllegalOp(); }
    default AtmState ejectCard()        { throw new IllegalOp(); }
}

// The dispenser: a small greedy problem, and it must be able to say no
class CashDispenser {
    private final NavigableMap<Integer, Integer> notes;   // denom -> count, desc

    synchronized Optional<Map<Integer,Integer>> plan(int amount) {
        Map<Integer,Integer> out = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        int remaining = amount;
        for (var e : notes.descendingMap().entrySet()) {
            int take = Math.min(remaining / e.getKey(), e.getValue());
            if (take > 0) { out.put(e.getKey(), take); remaining -= take * e.getKey(); }
        }
        return remaining == 0 ? Optional.of(out) : Optional.empty();  // refuse
    }
    // NOTE: greedy is optimal for {2000,500,200,100} but not for every
    // denomination set. Say so - DP is the general answer.

    synchronized void commit(Map<Integer,Integer> plan) {
        plan.forEach((denom, n) -> notes.merge(denom, -n, Integer::sum));
    }
}

// THE ORDERING THAT MATTERS
AtmState withdraw(Money amount) {
    var plan = dispenser.plan(amount.rupees())
                        .orElseThrow(CannotDispense::new);   // 1. CAN we?
    bank.debit(account, amount);                             // 2. debit FIRST
    try {
        dispenser.commit(plan);                              // 3. then dispense
        dispenser.push(plan);
    } catch (DispenseFailure e) {
        bank.credit(account, amount);                        // 4. COMPENSATE
        throw e;
    }
    return new Idle();
}
// Debit-then-dispense with compensation. Say why: an undetected
// dispense failure after a debit is the worst outcome.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • L84
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The whole game is a board of jumps, a set of players, a dice, and a turn loop. Keeping the jump lookup as a single map rather than two collections is the small insight.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Make the dice an interface so tests are deterministic. That single move shows you think about testability without being asked.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Small, but still a design
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              record Jump(int start, int end) {
    boolean isSnake()  { return end < start; }
}

class Board {
    private final int size;
    private final Map<Integer, Integer> jumps;     // ONE map, not two lists

    Board(int size, List<Jump> jumps) {
        this.size = size;
        this.jumps = jumps.stream()
            .collect(toMap(Jump::start, Jump::end));
    }
    int destinationFrom(int position) {
        return jumps.getOrDefault(position, position);   // snake or ladder
    }
}

interface Dice { int roll(); }                     // INTERFACE -> testable
class SixSidedDice implements Dice {
    public int roll() { return ThreadLocalRandom.current().nextInt(1, 7); }
}
class FixedDice implements Dice {                  // for tests
    private final Queue<Integer> rolls;
    public int roll() { return rolls.poll(); }
}

class Game {
    private final Board board;
    private final Dice dice;
    private final Deque<Player> turnOrder;

    Player play() {
        while (true) {
            Player p = turnOrder.poll();
            int roll = dice.roll();
            int next = p.position() + roll;

            if (next > board.size()) { turnOrder.add(p); continue; }  // overshoot
            next = board.destinationFrom(next);                       // jump
            p.moveTo(next);

            if (next == board.size()) return p;                       // won
            turnOrder.add(p);
        }
    }
}

// EXTENSIONS they may add: multiple dice, a bonus turn on a six,
// a snake at the last square. All are small changes to this shape.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              My notes

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • L85
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Model the piece hierarchy with movement rules on the pieces themselves — information expert — rather than a giant validator with a switch on piece type.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                For tic-tac-toe, checking only the row, column and diagonals through the last move is O(n) instead of O(n²). Mentioning that unprompted is a good signal.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Pieces own their moves
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                // TIC-TAC-TOE: check only through the LAST move, not the whole board
class Board {
    private final char[][] grid;
    private final int n;

    boolean isWinningMove(int r, int c, char sym) {
        boolean row = true, col = true, diag = true, anti = true;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            if (grid[r][i]     != sym) row  = false;
            if (grid[i][c]     != sym) col  = false;
            if (grid[i][i]     != sym) diag = false;
            if (grid[i][n-1-i] != sym) anti = false;
        }
        return row || col || (r == c && diag) || (r + c == n - 1 && anti);
    }   // O(n), not O(n^2)
}

// CHESS: the piece knows its own movement - information expert
abstract class Piece {
    protected final Color color;
    abstract boolean canMove(Board b, Square from, Square to);
}

class Knight extends Piece {
    boolean canMove(Board b, Square from, Square to) {
        int dr = Math.abs(from.row() - to.row());
        int dc = Math.abs(from.col() - to.col());
        return dr * dc == 2                                   // L shape
            && !b.at(to).map(p -> p.color == color).orElse(false);
    }
}
class Rook extends Piece {
    boolean canMove(Board b, Square from, Square to) {
        return (from.row() == to.row() || from.col() == to.col())
            && b.isPathClear(from, to);
    }
}

// The controller does NOT switch on piece type
class Game {
    void move(Square from, Square to) {
        Piece p = board.at(from).orElseThrow(NoPieceThere::new);
        if (p.color != currentTurn)        throw new NotYourTurn();
        if (!p.canMove(board, from, to))   throw new IllegalMove();
        if (wouldLeaveKingInCheck(p, from, to)) throw new IllegalMove();
        board.apply(from, to);
        currentTurn = currentTurn.opposite();
    }
}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • L86
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Fisher-Yates is the only correct in-place shuffle, and the range bound is where people get it wrong. Naming it and getting the bound right is a genuine signal.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Make the game rules a strategy so blackjack and poker share the deck. That is the extension the interviewer will ask for.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Deck, shuffle, and pluggable rules
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  enum Suit { HEARTS, DIAMONDS, CLUBS, SPADES }
enum Rank {
    TWO(2), THREE(3), /* ... */ JACK(10), QUEEN(10), KING(10), ACE(11);
    private final int value;
}
record Card(Rank rank, Suit suit) {}

class Deck {
    private final List<Card> cards = new ArrayList<>();

    Deck() {
        for (Suit s : Suit.values())
            for (Rank r : Rank.values())
                cards.add(new Card(r, s));       // 52, built once
    }

    void shuffle() {                             // Fisher-Yates
        var rnd = ThreadLocalRandom.current();
        for (int i = cards.size() - 1; i > 0; i--) {
            int j = rnd.nextInt(i + 1);          // INCLUSIVE of i - the bug spot
            Collections.swap(cards, i, j);
        }
    }
    Card deal() {
        if (cards.isEmpty()) throw new DeckEmpty();
        return cards.remove(cards.size() - 1);   // from the END: O(1)
    }
}

// THE AXIS THAT VARIES -> the game's rules
interface GameRules {
    int scoreHand(List<Card> hand);
    boolean shouldDeal(Player p);
    Optional<Player> winner(List<Player> players);
}
class BlackjackRules implements GameRules {
    public int scoreHand(List<Card> hand) {
        int total = hand.stream().mapToInt(c -> c.rank().value()).sum();
        long aces = hand.stream().filter(c -> c.rank() == ACE).count();
        while (total > 21 && aces-- > 0) total -= 10;   // ace as 1
        return total;
    }
}
class PokerRules implements GameRules { ... }

class CardGame {
    private final Deck deck; private final GameRules rules;   // swap the game
}

    private final MemberId member;
    private final LocalDate borrowedOn, dueOn;
    private LocalDate returnedOn;

    boolean isOverdue(LocalDate today) {
        return returnedOn == null && today.isAfter(dueOn);
    }
}

// RULES IN A POLICY, not scattered through the service
interface LendingPolicy {
    int maxConcurrentLoans(Member m);
    Period loanPeriod(Member m, BookItem item);
    Money finePerDay(Member m);
}
class StudentPolicy  implements LendingPolicy { /* 5 books, 14 days */ }
class FacultyPolicy  implements LendingPolicy { /* 20 books, 90 days */ }

class LendingService {
    Loan borrow(MemberId id, Isbn isbn) {
        Member m = members.byId(id).orElseThrow();
        if (loans.activeFor(id).size() >= policy.maxConcurrentLoans(m))
            throw new LoanLimitReached();
        if (fines.outstandingFor(id).isGreaterThan(MAX_DEBT))
            throw new FinesOutstanding();

        BookItem item = items.firstAvailable(isbn).orElseThrow(NoCopiesAvailable::new);
        item.markLoaned();                        // atomic in a transaction
        return loans.save(new Loan(item.barcode(), id, today,
                                   today.plus(policy.loanPeriod(m, item))));
    }
}

The mechanism must be atomic — a check followed by a write has a race.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Seat locking, with expiry
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      class SeatLock {
    private final SeatId seat;
    private final ShowId show;
    private final UserId user;
    private final Instant expiresAt;              // TEMPORARY - the key idea

    boolean isExpired() { return Instant.now().isAfter(expiresAt); }
}

class SeatLockService {
    private static final Duration HOLD = Duration.ofMinutes(10);

    // Atomic: the DB enforces it, not the application
    boolean tryLock(ShowId show, List<SeatId> seats, UserId user) {
        try {
            // UNIQUE (show_id, seat_id) on non-expired locks.
            // Two concurrent requests: one inserts, the other violates.
            locks.insertAll(seats.stream()
                .map(s -> new SeatLock(s, show, user, now().plus(HOLD)))
                .toList());
            return true;
        } catch (UniqueViolation e) {
            return false;                         // someone else got it
        }
    }
}

// Equivalent single-statement form:
//   UPDATE seats SET locked_by = :user, locked_until = now() + '10 min'
//   WHERE show_id = :show AND seat_id IN (:seats)
//     AND (locked_by IS NULL OR locked_until < now())
//   -> rows affected == seats.size() means you won ALL of them

class BookingService {
    Booking book(ShowId show, List<SeatId> seats, UserId user) {
        if (!lockService.tryLock(show, seats, user)) throw new SeatsUnavailable();
        try {
            var payment = payments.charge(user, price(show, seats));
            return bookings.confirm(show, seats, user, payment);   // lock -> booked
        } catch (PaymentFailed e) {
            lockService.release(show, seats, user);                // free at once
            throw e;
        }
        // If the user abandons: the lock EXPIRES. No cleanup job required
        // for correctness, though one is nice for freeing seats early.
    }
}

        if (pct.values().stream().reduce(ZERO, BigDecimal::add)
              .compareTo(new BigDecimal("100")) != 0)
            throw new PercentagesMustSumTo100();       // validate
        ...

class Expense {
    private final UserId paidBy;
    private final Money amount;
    private final Map<UserId, Money> owedBy;      // computed by the strategy
}

// NET BALANCE per person - positive = owed money, negative = owes
Map<UserId, Money> balances(List<Expense> expenses) {
    Map<UserId, Money> net = new HashMap<>();
    for (Expense e : expenses) {
        net.merge(e.paidBy(), e.amount(), Money::plus);
        e.owedBy().forEach((u, amt) -> net.merge(u, amt.negate(), Money::plus));
    }
    return net;
}

// SIMPLIFY: greedily match biggest creditor with biggest debtor
List<Transfer> simplify(Map<UserId, Money> net) {
    var creditors = new PriorityQueue<Entry>(comparing(Entry::amount).reversed());
    var debtors   = new PriorityQueue<Entry>(comparing(Entry::amount));
    net.forEach((u, m) -> (m.isPositive() ? creditors : debtors).add(new Entry(u, m)));

    List<Transfer> out = new ArrayList<>();
    while (!creditors.isEmpty() && !debtors.isEmpty()) {
        var c = creditors.poll(); var d = debtors.poll();
        Money amount = Money.min(c.amount(), d.amount().abs());
        out.add(new Transfer(d.user(), c.user(), amount));
        if (c.amount().isGreaterThan(amount)) creditors.add(c.minus(amount));
        if (d.amount().abs().isGreaterThan(amount)) debtors.add(d.plus(amount));
    }
    return out;
}
// SAY: "This is a greedy heuristic. Minimising the number of transfers
// exactly is NP-hard, and greedy is what every real app ships."

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • L90
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          A singly linked list will not do: removing a node requires its predecessor, which is O(n) to find. The doubly linked list is what makes eviction and promotion constant time.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Use sentinel head and tail nodes. They remove every null check from the pointer surgery, and pointer bugs are why people fail this question.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Hash map plus doubly linked list
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          class LRUCache<K, V> {
    private class Node {
        K key; V value; Node prev, next;
        Node(K key, V value) { this.key = key; this.value = value; }
    }

    private final int capacity;
    private final Map<K, Node> map = new HashMap<>();
    private final Node head = new Node(null, null);   // SENTINELS: no null checks
    private final Node tail = new Node(null, null);

    LRUCache(int capacity) {
        this.capacity = capacity;
        head.next = tail; tail.prev = head;
    }

    V get(K key) {
        Node n = map.get(key);
        if (n == null) return null;
        moveToFront(n);                               // mark as recently used
        return n.value;
    }

    void put(K key, V value) {
        Node existing = map.get(key);
        if (existing != null) {
            existing.value = value; moveToFront(existing); return;
        }
        if (map.size() == capacity) {
            Node lru = tail.prev;                     // least recent
            remove(lru); map.remove(lru.key);
        }
        Node n = new Node(key, value);
        map.put(key, n); addFirst(n);
    }

    private void remove(Node n) { n.prev.next = n.next; n.next.prev = n.prev; }
    private void addFirst(Node n) {
        n.next = head.next; n.prev = head;
        head.next.prev = n; head.next = n;
    }
    private void moveToFront(Node n) { remove(n); addFirst(n); }
}

Each is a separate axis, and conflating them is the common mistake.

An async appender with a bounded queue and a drop policy is the honest answer.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Levels, appenders, formatters
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            enum Level { TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR;
    boolean isAtLeast(Level min) { return ordinal() >= min.ordinal(); }
}

record LogEvent(Level level, String message, Instant at,
                String threadName, Throwable error) { }

interface Formatter { String format(LogEvent e); }      // HOW it looks
class PlainFormatter implements Formatter { ... }
class JsonFormatter  implements Formatter { ... }

interface Appender {                                    // WHERE it goes
    void append(LogEvent e);
}
class ConsoleAppender implements Appender {
    private final Formatter formatter;
    public void append(LogEvent e) { System.out.println(formatter.format(e)); }
}
class FileAppender     implements Appender { /* + rotation by size/date */ }

// ASYNC WRAPPER - the production-critical part
class AsyncAppender implements Appender {
    private final BlockingQueue<LogEvent> queue = new ArrayBlockingQueue<>(10_000);
    private final Appender delegate;

    public void append(LogEvent e) {
        if (!queue.offer(e)) droppedCount.increment();   // DROP, never block
    }
    // a single daemon thread drains the queue into the delegate
}

class Logger {
    private final Level minLevel;
    private final List<Appender> appenders;

    void log(Level level, String msg, Throwable t) {
        if (!level.isAtLeast(minLevel)) return;          // cheap early exit
        var event = new LogEvent(level, msg, Instant.now(),
                                 Thread.currentThread().getName(), t);
        for (Appender a : appenders) {
            try { a.append(event); }
            catch (Throwable ignored) { }                // logging NEVER throws
        }
    }
}
