Fallback between channels is the requirement people forget.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Say something about deduplication and rate limiting per user — sending forty push notifications in a minute is a product failure that the design should prevent.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Channels, templates, fallback
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              interface NotificationChannel {
    ChannelType type();
    boolean supports(User u);                   // has the user a phone? consented?
    DeliveryResult send(User u, RenderedMessage m);
}
class EmailChannel implements NotificationChannel { ... }
class SmsChannel   implements NotificationChannel { ... }
class PushChannel  implements NotificationChannel { ... }
class InAppChannel implements NotificationChannel { ... }

interface TemplateEngine { RenderedMessage render(NotificationType t, ChannelType c, Map<String,Object> data); }
// one template PER (type, channel): an SMS is not a truncated email

class NotificationService {
    private final Map<ChannelType, NotificationChannel> channels;
    private final PreferenceStore preferences;
    private final RateLimiter limiter;
    private final DedupeStore dedupe;

    void notify(UserId userId, NotificationType type, Map<String,Object> data) {
        User u = users.byId(userId);

        if (!preferences.wants(u, type))            return;       // opted out
        if (dedupe.seenRecently(u, type, data))     return;       // duplicate
        if (!limiter.allow(u))                      { queue.deferred(u, type, data); return; }

        // ORDERED fallback - try the preferred channel, then the next
        for (ChannelType ct : preferences.channelOrder(u, type)) {
            var channel = channels.get(ct);
            if (channel == null || !channel.supports(u)) continue;

            var msg = templates.render(type, ct, data);
            var result = channel.send(u, msg);

            if (result.isSuccess()) { audit.record(u, type, ct); return; }
            if (result.isPermanentFailure()) continue;   // bad number: next channel
            // transient: the retry policy handles it, do not fall through
            return;
        }
        audit.recordUndeliverable(u, type);
    }
}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Make the strategy an interface — token bucket, leaky bucket, sliding window, fixed window — so the policy is swappable. Then handle the map of per-user buckets growing without bound.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The memory leak is the detail that separates answers. A ConcurrentHashMap keyed by user id, never evicted, is an unbounded leak in a service with many users.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Per-user, thread-safe, bounded
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                interface RateLimitStrategy {
    boolean tryAcquire(int permits);
}

class TokenBucketStrategy implements RateLimitStrategy {
    private final long capacity; private final double refillPerSec;
    private double tokens; private long lastNanos;

    public synchronized boolean tryAcquire(int permits) {
        refill();
        if (tokens >= permits) { tokens -= permits; return true; }
        return false;
    }
    private void refill() {
        long now = System.nanoTime();
        tokens = Math.min(capacity, tokens + (now - lastNanos) / 1e9 * refillPerSec);
        lastNanos = now;                        // lazy: no background timer
    }
}

class SlidingWindowLog implements RateLimitStrategy {
    private final Deque<Long> timestamps = new ArrayDeque<>();
    private final int limit; private final long windowNanos;

    public synchronized boolean tryAcquire(int permits) {
        long now = System.nanoTime(), cutoff = now - windowNanos;
        while (!timestamps.isEmpty() && timestamps.peekFirst() < cutoff)
            timestamps.pollFirst();             // evict old
        if (timestamps.size() + permits > limit) return false;
        for (int i = 0; i < permits; i++) timestamps.addLast(now);
        return true;
    }   // exact, but O(limit) memory per key
}

class RateLimiter {
    // BOUNDED - this is the part people miss
    private final Cache<UserId, RateLimitStrategy> buckets = Caffeine.newBuilder()
        .maximumSize(1_000_000)
        .expireAfterAccess(Duration.ofMinutes(10))    // idle users evicted
        .build();

    private final Supplier<RateLimitStrategy> factory;

    boolean allow(UserId user) {
        return buckets.get(user, k -> factory.get()).tryAcquire(1);
    }
}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Composite, plus the sharp edges
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  abstract class FsNode {
    protected String name;
    protected Directory parent;
    protected Instant modifiedAt;
    protected Permissions permissions;

    abstract long size();
    String path() {
        return parent == null ? "/" + name : parent.path() + "/" + name;
    }
}

class FileNode extends FsNode {
    private byte[] content;
    long size() { return content.length; }
}

class Directory extends FsNode {
    private final Map<String, FsNode> children = new LinkedHashMap<>();

    void add(FsNode n) {
        if (children.containsKey(n.name)) throw new AlreadyExists(n.name);
        n.parent = this; children.put(n.name, n);
    }
    long size() {                                   // RECURSION is the point
        return children.values().stream().mapToLong(FsNode::size).sum();
    }
    Optional<FsNode> resolve(String path) {
        var parts = path.split("/");
        FsNode current = this;
        for (String part : parts) {
            if (part.isEmpty() || part.equals("."))  continue;
            if (part.equals("..")) { current = current.parent; continue; }
            if (!(current instanceof Directory d))   return Optional.empty();
            current = d.children.get(part);
            if (current == null)                     return Optional.empty();
        }
        return Optional.of(current);
    }
}

// SYMLINK - turns the TREE into a GRAPH. Cycles become possible.
class SymLink extends FsNode {
    private final String target;
    long size() { return target.length(); }         // the link, not the target
}

long sizeWithLinks(FsNode n, Set<FsNode> visiting) {
    if (!visiting.add(n)) throw new SymlinkLoop(n.path());   // CYCLE DETECTION
    try { return n.size(); } finally { visiting.remove(n); }
}

// SEARCH via Visitor, so new operations do not edit the node classes
interface FsVisitor<R> { R visitFile(FileNode f); R visitDir(Directory d); }

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • L95
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A typing command knows what it inserted and where, so undo is a delete — cheap and precise. A 'reformat entire document' operation has no clean inverse, so snapshot the state instead.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The refinement that shows experience: coalescing consecutive keystrokes into one command, so undo does not step back one character at a time.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Command, Memento, and coalescing
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    interface EditCommand {
    void execute(Document doc);
    void undo(Document doc);
    default boolean coalesceWith(EditCommand next) { return false; }
}

class InsertText implements EditCommand {
    private final int position;
    private StringBuilder text;                  // mutable: allows coalescing

    public void execute(Document d) { d.insert(position, text.toString()); }
    public void undo(Document d)    { d.delete(position, position + text.length()); }

    // Typing "hello" should be ONE undo, not five
    public boolean coalesceWith(EditCommand next) {
        if (next instanceof InsertText ins
            && ins.position == this.position + this.text.length()
            && !ins.text.toString().contains("\n")) {      // break on newline
            this.text.append(ins.text);
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
}

// NOT cleanly reversible -> Memento
class ReformatDocument implements EditCommand {
    private Document.Snapshot before;
    public void execute(Document d) { before = d.snapshot(); d.reformat(); }
    public void undo(Document d)    { d.restore(before); }
}

class UndoManager {
    private final Deque<EditCommand> undo = new ArrayDeque<>();
    private final Deque<EditCommand> redo = new ArrayDeque<>();
    private final int maxDepth = 100;            // bound the memory

    void run(EditCommand cmd, Document doc) {
        cmd.execute(doc);
        var last = undo.peek();
        if (last == null || !last.coalesceWith(cmd)) {
            undo.push(cmd);
            if (undo.size() > maxDepth) undo.removeLast();   // bounded
        }
        redo.clear();                            // a new action kills the branch
    }
}

// use commands for the common case and snapshot only occasionally.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • L96
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Finding a common free slot across attendees is a sweep: merge everyone's busy intervals, then look for gaps of the required length. That is the answer to 'find a time that works for all five'.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Recurring events should be stored as a rule plus exceptions, not as expanded instances — expanding 'every Monday forever' is not possible.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Intervals, sweeps, and recurrence
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      record TimeSlot(Instant start, Instant end) {
    boolean overlaps(TimeSlot o) {
        return start.isBefore(o.end) && o.start.isBefore(end);   // strict
    }
}

// FIND A COMMON FREE SLOT - merge busy intervals, then find the gaps
List<TimeSlot> freeSlots(List<Attendee> attendees, TimeSlot window, Duration need) {
    List<TimeSlot> busy = attendees.stream()
        .flatMap(a -> a.busyIn(window).stream())
        .sorted(comparing(TimeSlot::start))
        .toList();

    List<TimeSlot> merged = new ArrayList<>();          // merge overlaps
    for (TimeSlot s : busy) {
        if (!merged.isEmpty() && !merged.get(merged.size()-1).end().isBefore(s.start()))
            merged.set(merged.size()-1, new TimeSlot(
                merged.get(merged.size()-1).start(),
                max(merged.get(merged.size()-1).end(), s.end())));
        else merged.add(s);
    }

    List<TimeSlot> free = new ArrayList<>();            // gaps between them
    Instant cursor = window.start();
    for (TimeSlot b : merged) {
        if (Duration.between(cursor, b.start()).compareTo(need) >= 0)
            free.add(new TimeSlot(cursor, b.start()));
        cursor = max(cursor, b.end());
    }
    if (Duration.between(cursor, window.end()).compareTo(need) >= 0)
        free.add(new TimeSlot(cursor, window.end()));
    return free;
}

// RECURRENCE - a RULE, never expanded instances
record RecurrenceRule(Frequency freq, int interval, Set<DayOfWeek> byDay,
                      LocalDate until, Integer count) { }   // RFC 5545 (iCal)

class RecurringEvent {
    private final RecurrenceRule rule;
    private final Set<LocalDate> exceptions;        // deleted occurrences
    private final Map<LocalDate, Event> overrides;  // "this one moved to 3pm"

    Stream<Event> occurrencesBetween(LocalDate from, LocalDate to) {
        return rule.datesBetween(from, to)
                   .filter(d -> !exceptions.contains(d))
                   .map(d -> overrides.getOrDefault(d, materialise(d)));
    }
}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The concurrency question is the same as seat booking: two riders must not be matched to one driver. A conditional update on driver status is the answer.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        // 1. MATCHING - a geo index, not a full scan
interface DriverLocationIndex {
    List<DriverId> nearby(Location l, double radiusKm);   // geohash / quadtree
    void update(DriverId d, Location l);                  // high write rate
}

interface MatchingStrategy {
    Optional<DriverId> match(RideRequest r, List<DriverId> candidates);
}
class NearestDriver    implements MatchingStrategy { ... }
class HighestRated     implements MatchingStrategy { ... }
class FairDistribution implements MatchingStrategy { /* earnings equity */ }

// 2. PRICING - Strategy, and surge composes as a Decorator
interface PricingStrategy { Money quote(Route route, Instant at); }

class BasePricing implements PricingStrategy { /* base + per km + per min */ }

class SurgePricing implements PricingStrategy {
    private final PricingStrategy inner;
    private final SurgeCalculator surge;
    public Money quote(Route r, Instant at) {
        return inner.quote(r, at).times(surge.multiplierFor(r.origin(), at));
    }
}

// 3. TRIP - a State machine with strictly ordered transitions
enum TripStatus { REQUESTED, MATCHED, DRIVER_ARRIVING, IN_PROGRESS,
                  COMPLETED, CANCELLED }

class Trip {
    private TripStatus status = REQUESTED;
    void driverAccepted(DriverId d) { require(REQUESTED);       status = MATCHED; }
    void start()                    { require(DRIVER_ARRIVING); status = IN_PROGRESS; }
    void complete(Money fare)       { require(IN_PROGRESS);     status = COMPLETED; }

    private void require(TripStatus expected) {
        if (status != expected) throw new IllegalTransition(status, expected);
    }
}

//   WHERE id=:driver AND status='AVAILABLE'

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • L98
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The state machine has more actors than the ride-hailing one, and a cancellation means something different at each stage. Model who is allowed to cancel when, and what the compensation is.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Menu modelling matters too: a restaurant's items change over time, while past orders must still render correctly. That forces a snapshot of name and price on the order line.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Multi-party state machine
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          enum OrderStatus {
    PLACED,             // customer paid
    ACCEPTED,           // restaurant confirmed
    PREPARING,
    READY_FOR_PICKUP,
    PARTNER_ASSIGNED,
    PICKED_UP,
    DELIVERED,
    CANCELLED
}

class Order {
    private OrderStatus status = PLACED;
    private final List<OrderItem> items;

    // Each party advances it, and only from legal states
    void restaurantAccepts()          { require(PLACED);           status = ACCEPTED; }
    void markReady()                  { require(PREPARING);        status = READY_FOR_PICKUP; }
    void partnerAssigned(PartnerId p) { require(READY_FOR_PICKUP); status = PARTNER_ASSIGNED; }
    void pickedUp()                   { require(PARTNER_ASSIGNED); status = PICKED_UP; }
    void delivered()                  { require(PICKED_UP);        status = DELIVERED; }

    // WHO may cancel, and WHEN - the interesting rule
    void cancelByCustomer() {
        if (status.ordinal() >= PICKED_UP.ordinal())
            throw new TooLateToCancel();
        if (status.ordinal() >= PREPARING.ordinal())
            refunds.partial(this);        // food already being made
        else
            refunds.full(this);
        status = CANCELLED;
    }
}

}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • L99
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The bid check — is this higher than the current highest — followed by the write is a classic read-modify-write race. A conditional update or a version column solves it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Closing is the subtler part: a scheduled job and a lazy check on read can both fire. Make close() idempotent so it does not matter which wins.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Bidding races and idempotent close
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            class Auction {
    private final ItemId item;
    private final Instant endsAt;
    private final Money reservePrice;
    private volatile AuctionStatus status = OPEN;
    private Bid highestBid;

    // THE RACE: two bids at once must not both "win"
    synchronized Bid placeBid(UserId bidder, Money amount) {
        if (status != OPEN)                  throw new AuctionClosed();
        if (Instant.now().isAfter(endsAt))   { close(); throw new AuctionClosed(); }
        if (highestBid != null && !amount.isGreaterThan(highestBid.amount()))
                                             throw new BidTooLow(highestBid.amount());
        if (amount.isLessThan(reservePrice)) throw new BelowReserve();

        var previous = highestBid;
        this.highestBid = new Bid(bidder, amount, Instant.now());
        if (previous != null)
            events.publish(new Outbid(previous.bidder(), item));   // notify loser
        return highestBid;
    }

    // IDEMPOTENT: a scheduler AND a lazy read-check may both call this
    synchronized void close() {
        if (status != OPEN) return;                    // already closed - fine
        status = CLOSED;
        if (highestBid == null || highestBid.amount().isLessThan(reservePrice))
            events.publish(new AuctionEndedUnsold(item));
        else
            events.publish(new AuctionWon(item, highestBid));
    }
}

// DISTRIBUTED: `synchronized` does not survive multiple instances.
// Use a conditional update instead:
//
//   UPDATE auctions
//   SET highest_bid = :amount, highest_bidder = :user, version = version + 1
//   WHERE id = :id AND status = 'OPEN' AND ends_at > now()
//     AND (highest_bid IS NULL OR highest_bid < :amount)
//
//   0 rows affected -> you were outbid or it closed. Re-read and retry.

// MENTION: anti-sniping (extend the end time if a bid lands in the last
// 30 seconds) and proxy bidding (auto-bid up to a hidden maximum).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              A two-phase model works: reserve on add-to-cart with a TTL, commit on payment. Available stock is physical stock minus active reservations, derived rather than stored twice.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The atomic decrement with a guard is the mechanism, and it is the whole answer: zero rows affected means insufficient stock, with no race between the check and the write.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Reserve, expire, commit
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              class Inventory {
    private final SkuId sku;
    private int physicalStock;      // what is actually in the warehouse
    private int reserved;           // held by open carts

    int available() { return physicalStock - reserved; }   // DERIVED
}

class Reservation {
    private final ReservationId id;
    private final SkuId sku;
    private final int quantity;
    private final Instant expiresAt;      // TTL - abandoned carts free stock
    private ReservationStatus status;     // HELD, COMMITTED, RELEASED, EXPIRED
}

class InventoryService {
    private static final Duration HOLD = Duration.ofMinutes(15);

    // ATOMIC check-and-decrement. This one statement IS the answer.
    Reservation reserve(SkuId sku, int qty, CartId cart) {
        int updated = jdbc.update(
            "UPDATE inventory SET reserved = reserved + ? " +
            "WHERE sku = ? AND (physical_stock - reserved) >= ?",
            qty, sku, qty);

        if (updated == 0) throw new InsufficientStock(sku, qty);   // no race
        return reservations.save(
            new Reservation(sku, qty, cart, now().plus(HOLD)));
    }

    @Transactional
    void commit(ReservationId id) {                 // payment succeeded
        var r = reservations.byId(id).orElseThrow();
        if (r.isExpired()) throw new ReservationExpired();
        jdbc.update("UPDATE inventory SET physical_stock = physical_stock - ?, " +
                    "reserved = reserved - ? WHERE sku = ?",
                    r.qty(), r.qty(), r.sku());
        r.markCommitted();
    }

    void release(ReservationId id) {                // cart abandoned / payment failed
        var r = reservations.byId(id).orElseThrow();
        jdbc.update("UPDATE inventory SET reserved = reserved - ? WHERE sku = ?",
                    r.qty(), r.sku());
        r.markReleased();
    }
}

Idempotency keys so retries are safe. Webhooks for the async result, because a timeout does not mean the charge failed.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The state machine needs an UNKNOWN state. A timeout leaves the payment in a state you must reconcile with the provider rather than guess at — assuming failure is how you double-charge.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Adapter, idempotency, webhooks
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                interface PaymentGateway {                          // YOUR vocabulary
    AuthorizationResult authorize(PaymentRequest r);
    CaptureResult capture(AuthorizationId id, Money amount);
    RefundResult refund(TransactionId id, Money amount, String reason);
}
class StripeGateway   implements PaymentGateway { /* Adapter over the SDK */ }
class RazorpayGateway implements PaymentGateway { ... }

enum PaymentStatus {
    INITIATED, AUTHORIZED, CAPTURED, FAILED, REFUNDED,
    UNKNOWN                     // <- timeout. This state MUST exist.
}

class PaymentService {

    @Transactional
    Payment pay(OrderId order, Money amount, IdempotencyKey key) {
        // 1. Idempotency - a retry returns the ORIGINAL result
        var existing = payments.byIdempotencyKey(key);
        if (existing.isPresent()) return existing.get();

        // 2. Record BEFORE calling out, so a crash still leaves a trace
        var payment = payments.save(Payment.initiated(order, amount, key));

        try {
            var auth = gateway.authorize(new PaymentRequest(amount, key));
            payment.authorized(auth.id());
        } catch (TimeoutException e) {
            payment.markUnknown();               // NOT failed. We do not know.
            reconciliation.enqueue(payment);     // ask the provider later
            throw new PaymentPending();
        }
        return payments.save(payment);
    }

    // 3. WEBHOOK - the async source of truth
    void onWebhook(WebhookEvent e) {
        if (!signatures.verify(e))       throw new InvalidSignature();  // ALWAYS
        if (processed.contains(e.id()))  return;   // webhooks are at-least-once

        var payment = payments.byProviderRef(e.reference()).orElseThrow();
        switch (e.type()) {
            case "charge.succeeded" -> payment.captured(e.amount());
            case "charge.failed"    -> payment.failed(e.reason());
            case "charge.refunded"  -> payment.refunded(e.amount());
        }
        processed.add(e.id());
    }
}

// THE THREE SENTENCES THAT SCORE
//   "A timeout is UNKNOWN, not failed - reconcile, never assume."
//   "Idempotency keys make retries safe."
//   "Webhooks are at-least-once and their signature must be verified."''

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • L102
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  A counter encoded in base62 is collision-free by construction and produces short codes — but sequential ones, which leak your volume and are enumerable. A hash is unguessable but needs collision handling.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Custom aliases are what force a real design: user-chosen codes must not collide with generated ones, which means one atomic uniqueness check covering both.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Encoding and collisions
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  interface CodeGenerator { String generate(String longUrl); }

// OPTION 1: counter + base62 - no collisions possible, but sequential
class CounterBase62 implements CodeGenerator {
    private static final String ALPHABET =
        "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ";
    private final IdAllocator ids;              // DB sequence, or a range block

    public String generate(String longUrl) {
        long id = ids.next();
        var sb = new StringBuilder();
        do { sb.append(ALPHABET.charAt((int) (id % 62))); id /= 62; } while (id > 0);
        return sb.reverse().toString();
    }
    // 62^7 = 3.5 trillion codes in 7 characters
    // -: sequential -> enumerable, and leaks how many links exist
    // FIX: multiply the counter by a large coprime mod 62^n to scramble it
}

// OPTION 2: hash + check - unguessable, needs retry on collision
class HashBased implements CodeGenerator {
    public String generate(String longUrl) {
        for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 5; attempt++) {
            String candidate = base62(sha256(longUrl + attempt)).substring(0, 7);
            if (repo.putIfAbsent(candidate, longUrl)) return candidate;   // atomic
        }
        throw new CouldNotGenerate();
    }
}

class ShortenerService {
    ShortLink shorten(String longUrl, Optional<String> alias, UserId owner) {
        String code = alias
            .map(this::validateAlias)        // reserved words, length, charset
            .orElseGet(() -> generator.generate(longUrl));

        // ONE uniqueness check covers generated AND custom codes
        if (!repo.putIfAbsent(code, longUrl)) throw new AliasTaken(code);
        return new ShortLink(code, longUrl, owner, Instant.now(), expiry);
    }

    String resolve(String code) {
        var link = cache.get(code, k -> repo.byCode(k).orElseThrow(NotFound::new));
        if (link.isExpired()) throw new LinkExpired();
        analytics.recordAsync(code);         // ASYNC - never block the redirect
        return link.longUrl();
    }
}

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • L103
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Persist first, then push. The message store is the source of truth and the websocket is only a fast path — otherwise a disconnected user silently loses messages.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Group chat changes the fan-out: one message, N recipients, N delivery statuses. Say whether you store a row per recipient or a read cursor per user, and why the cursor scales better.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Rooms, delivery status, offline
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    enum DeliveryStatus { SENT, DELIVERED, READ, FAILED }

record Message(MessageId id, RoomId room, UserId sender,
               String body, long sequence, Instant sentAt) { }
//                          ^ server-assigned per room. NEVER order by
//                            client timestamps - clocks disagree.

interface ConnectionRegistry {                 // who is online, and where
    Optional<Session> sessionFor(UserId u);
    void register(UserId u, Session s);
    void unregister(UserId u);
}

class ChatService {

    void send(RoomId room, UserId sender, String body) {
        var msg = messages.save(Message.of(room, sender, body, nextSeq(room)));
        //        ^ PERSIST FIRST. The store is the source of truth;
        //          the socket is only a fast path.

        for (UserId recipient : rooms.membersOf(room)) {
            if (recipient.equals(sender)) continue;

            registry.sessionFor(recipient).ifPresentOrElse(
                session -> {
                    session.push(msg);                       // online
                    cursors.markDelivered(recipient, msg.sequence());
                },
                () -> push.notify(recipient, msg)            // offline
            );                                               // fetched on reconnect
        }
    }

    // On reconnect: everything after their last acknowledged sequence
    List<Message> sync(UserId user, RoomId room) {
        long lastSeen = cursors.deliveredUpTo(user, room);
        var pending = messages.after(room, lastSeen);
        if (!pending.isEmpty())
            cursors.markDelivered(user, pending.get(pending.size()-1).sequence());
        return pending;
    }

    void markRead(UserId user, RoomId room, long upTo) {
        cursors.markRead(user, room, upTo);
        rooms.notifySender(room, new ReadReceipt(user, upTo));   // Observer
    }
}

// THE DESIGN CALL TO STATE
//   a delivery row per recipient   -> N rows per message, exact, heavy
//   a read cursor per user+room    -> 1 row per user, scales to large groups
//   Cursors are what real systems use.

// AND: typing indicators are ephemeral - never persist them.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Level 8
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The interview round itself
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Days 51-54
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Done whenYou can run a 45-minute machine coding round to a working, defensible design - and extend it live when the interviewer adds a requirement.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    StudyAwesome LLD - problems and solutions →Code smells catalog →
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    0/8
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • L104
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Most candidates optimise for pattern count and lose points on the other three. A design with two well-placed interfaces and running code beats one with eight patterns that does not compile.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The extensibility test is almost always applied live: they add a requirement in the last ten minutes and watch how much you have to change.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      What the rubric usually is
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      TYPICAL WEIGHTING

  WORKING CODE      it compiles and runs the happy path          ~30%
                    (an elegant design that never ran scores badly)

  EXTENSIBILITY     the "now add X" test in the last 10 minutes  ~30%
                    one new class, nothing else edited   = pass
                    edits across five files              = fail

  CORRECTNESS       the edge cases THEY name                     ~20%
                    concurrency where it obviously matters
                    (two cars/one spot, two bids/one item)

  COMMUNICATION     stated assumptions, narrated trade-offs,     ~20%
                    asked before assuming

NOT HEAVILY WEIGHTED
  the number of patterns used
  perfect UML
  getters and setters written out in full
  a database schema, unless they asked for one

// HIGHEST-LEVERAGE HABIT: 5 minutes on requirements, then write the
// INTERFACES before any implementation. An interviewer can read the
// entire design off the interfaces alone - and if you run out of time,
// the design is still complete on screen.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Saved links

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • L105
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Ask about scope, scale, concurrency and persistence. Then write the answers down as a short list — it becomes your contract and stops scope drift halfway through the implementation.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        If the interviewer says you decide, decide out loud in one sentence and move on. Hesitating over an unimportant choice burns the clock you need for code.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The five minutes that decide the round
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        ASK THESE, IN THIS ORDER

  SCOPE        "Should I handle payments, or assume a separate service
                I can call?"     "One lot, or multiple locations?"

  SCALE        "In-memory for this exercise, or design as if distributed?"
               -> this ONE answer changes the whole design

  CONCURRENCY  "Multiple users at once? Should I handle two people
                picking the same seat?"
               -> they almost always say yes, and it is a scored point

  PERSISTENCE  "In-memory collections, or should I sketch repositories?"

  EXTENSION    "Any variations you'd like the design to support?"
               -> this is them TELLING you what they will ask for
                  later. Listen very carefully to the answer.

THEN WRITE IT DOWN, VISIBLY:

  // ASSUMPTIONS
  // - single parking lot, multiple floors
  // - in-memory storage, behind repository interfaces
  // - concurrent entry: two vehicles must not get the same spot
  // - pricing: hourly, varies by vehicle size
  // - OUT OF SCOPE: payments, auth, reservations, persistence

// "Out of scope" matters as much as "in scope". It stops them
// wondering why something is missing, and stops you drifting into it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        My notes
