                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • L106
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Interviewers are watching for prioritisation. Naming the thing you are skipping, and saying roughly how you would add it, earns most of the credit for having thought about it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Stub the excluded parts behind an interface rather than ignoring them. The seam is what demonstrates you know where it would go.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Excluding deliberately
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          SAY IT, DO NOT JUST OMIT IT

  "I'm stubbing persistence behind a repository interface rather than
   writing JDBC, so the design shows the seam without spending time
   on plumbing."

  "I'll skip authentication - assuming a UserId arrives from upstream."

  "I'm handling the two error cases that affect the DESIGN (lot full,
   invalid ticket) and leaving general exception handling out."

STUB IT VISIBLY - the seam earns the credit
  interface OrderRepository {
      void save(Order o);
      Optional<Order> byId(OrderId id);
  }
  class InMemoryOrderRepository implements OrderRepository {
      private final Map<OrderId, Order> store = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
      public void save(Order o) { store.put(o.id(), o); }
      public Optional<Order> byId(OrderId id) {
          return Optional.ofNullable(store.get(id));
      }
  }   // 6 lines, actually works, and shows where the database goes

ALWAYS INCLUDE, EVEN WHEN SHORT ON TIME
  the interfaces            (they ARE the design)
  the one or two concurrency points that matter
  a main() that RUNS the happy path

CUT FIRST
  getters/setters ("assume standard accessors")
  full equals/hashCode (say it; write it if asked)
  validation on every parameter
  logging

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • L107
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The useful narration is trade-offs: what you considered, what you chose, and what would change your mind. It is the only way an interviewer learns whether you understand the design or memorised it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Write interfaces first, then implementations. It shows the whole shape early and leaves you with a complete design on screen even if you run short.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            What to say while you type
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            SAY THIS                                  NOT THIS
"Allocation is a Strategy because you     "Now I'll create a class
 mentioned nearest-first, and I expect     called SpotAllocator..."
 a different rule later."

"This is synchronized because two          "Adding synchronized here."
 vehicles can arrive at once and both
 see the same free spot."

"I'm using an enum for VehicleSize          (silence)
 rather than a hierarchy - there's no
 behaviour that differs, only ordering."

"I'd normally put this behind a             (just not doing it)
 repository; I'll use a Map and mark
 where persistence goes."

ORDER OF WORK IN 45 MINUTES
  1. assumptions, written down            2 min
  2. INTERFACES, enums, records           8 min   <- the design, visible
  3. core implementation                 20 min
  4. main() running the happy path        5 min
  5. narrate what you would add next      5 min
                                          5 min buffer

// Interfaces first means that even if you run out of time, the DESIGN
// is complete on screen - and the design is what is being scored.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • L108
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Before you code, guess what they will add. For a parking lot it is a pricing rule or a vehicle type. For an elevator it is a scheduling policy. Put the interface there in advance.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              If the new requirement genuinely does not fit, say so and describe the refactor with its rough cost. That reads far better than forcing a boolean flag through three classes.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Passing the extension test
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              THE ASK USUALLY LANDS ON A PREDICTABLE AXIS

  parking lot    -> "now add EV charging spots"
                 -> "now pricing differs at weekends"
  elevator       -> "now prioritise the executive floor"
  vending        -> "now support card payment"
  notification   -> "now add WhatsApp"
  rate limiter   -> "now per-endpoint, not per-user"

// If you put a Strategy on that axis, the answer is ONE CLASS:
class WeekendPricing implements PricingStrategy {
    private final PricingStrategy base;
    public Money price(Duration d, VehicleSize s) {
        return base.price(d, s).times(1.5);
    }
}
// "That's it - I pass a different strategy at construction.
//  Nothing existing changes."          <- the sentence you want to say

// IF IT GENUINELY DOESN'T FIT, BE HONEST AND COST IT
"That doesn't fit cleanly. I assumed one vehicle per spot, and charging
 means a spot has a resource that outlives the parking session. I'd
 extract a SpotResource abstraction - Spot holds a list of them, and
 the allocator filters on required resources. That's about a 20-minute
 refactor touching Spot and the allocator."

// Naming the refactor and its cost scores far better than hacking an
// isElectric boolean into three classes and hoping.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Saved links

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • L109
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Over-engineering is the strong candidate's failure — abstract factories on a problem that needed two interfaces. Under-engineering is the weaker one's: a single class doing everything.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Two checks catch both. For every interface, can you name a second implementation that is plausibly needed? For every class, can you describe it without the word 'and'?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The four losses
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                1. OVER-ENGINEERING       (the strong-candidate failure)
   AbstractSpotFactoryProvider, a Visitor over 3 classes, an event
   bus in a single-threaded exercise.
   CHECK: "can I name a second implementation that is plausibly needed?"
          No -> delete the interface. Use a concrete class.

2. NO INTERFACES AT ALL   (the weak-candidate failure)
   Everything concrete, pricing as an if/else chain, no seam anywhere.
   CHECK: "when they add a requirement, how many files do I edit?"
          More than one -> an interface is missing.

3. GOD CLASS
   ParkingLotManager doing parking, pricing, payment, reporting.
   CHECK: "can I describe this class without saying 'and'?"

4. IT NEVER RAN
   45 minutes of beautiful interfaces, no main(), nothing executed.
   Always reserve the last 5 minutes.

ALSO COMMON
   anemic model      all logic in services, entities are field bags
   no encapsulation  public fields, or a setter for every invariant
   ignored the race  "two cars at once" asked, and no answer given
   wrong types       double for money, String for status
   magic strings     no enums for a fixed set of states

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • L110
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Interviewers are not counting patterns; they are checking whether you know when one is warranted. Saying this could be a Strategy, but there is only one rule, so I will extract it when a second appears demonstrates exactly the judgment being tested.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  When you do use one, name it and say what it buys. An unnamed Strategy looks accidental rather than chosen.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  When a plain class wins
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  USE A PATTERN WHEN
  you can NAME the second implementation   "card, UPI and wallet fees"
  the interviewer hinted at variation      "rates might change later"
  the alternative is a switch that will keep growing
  it removes duplication that already exists

USE A PLAIN CLASS WHEN
  there is one implementation and no second one in sight
  the "variation" is hypothetical
  the pattern adds a file to save two lines

SAY THIS OUT LOUD - it scores:
  "Ticket creation could be a Factory, but there's only one kind of
   ticket and I can't name a second, so I'll keep the constructor.
   If we added season passes I'd extract a factory then."

  "Pricing IS a Strategy, because you said rates vary by vehicle type
   and I expect weekend or peak pricing to come next."

THE INVERSE MISTAKE - a pattern with no explanation:
  an interface with exactly one implementation and no comment reads
  as accidental. Name the pattern and say what it buys, or drop it.

// YAGNI applies in interviews too. Knowing that IS the signal.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  My notes

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • L111
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A main() that parks a car, prints the ticket, unparks and prints the fee proves more than another interface would. It also often surfaces a bug you can fix in front of them, which reads well.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    If there is no time to run it, say the test cases you would write. Naming them shows you thought about correctness even when the clock beat you.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Prove it works
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    // THE LAST FIVE MINUTES - always
public static void main(String[] args) {
    var lot = new ParkingLot(
        List.of(new Floor(1, List.of(new Spot("1-A", COMPACT),
                                     new Spot("1-B", LARGE)))),
        new NearestFirstAllocation(),
        new HourlyPricing());

    Ticket t = lot.park(new Vehicle("MH12AB1234", COMPACT));
    System.out.println("parked at " + t.spot().id());        // 1-A

    Money fee = lot.unpark(t);
    System.out.println("fee " + fee);                        // Rs 40

    // and the failure path - shows you thought past the happy case
    try {
        lot.park(new Vehicle("X", LARGE));
        lot.park(new Vehicle("Y", LARGE));
        System.out.println("BUG: should have rejected");
    } catch (LotFull e) {
        System.out.println("correctly rejected when full");
    }
}

// NO TIME TO RUN IT? NAME THE TESTS - takes 45 seconds to say:
"Tests I'd write:
   - park with a suitable spot free        -> ticket issued
   - park when the lot is full             -> LotFull
   - park LARGE when only COMPACT is free  -> LotFull
   - unpark computes the fee from elapsed time
   - two threads parking at once           -> different spots
   - unpark with an already-used ticket    -> rejected"

// That demonstrates you thought about correctness even if the clock won.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    React
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    It is on your resume, so it is fair game - and depth here opens full-stack Software Engineer roles where your backend experience becomes the differentiator.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Foundations
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Days 1-5
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Done whenYou can explain what happens between a click and a repainted pixel, in React's own terms, without hand-waving.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Studyreact.dev — Render and commit →react.dev — Preserving and resetting state →
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    0/13
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • R01
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      <Foo bar=1 /> becomes jsx(Foo, {bar:1}), which returns a description object — not a DOM node, and not a rendered component. React decides later what to do with it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Capitalisation is what tells the compiler the difference between a DOM tag and your component. And children is just another prop, which is why you can pass it explicitly or as JSX between the tags.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      What JSX compiles to
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      <Button size="lg">Save</Button>
// becomes
jsx(Button, { size: "lg", children: "Save" })

// lowercase -> DOM tag as a string; Capitalised -> your component
<div />      -> jsx("div", {})
<Div />      -> jsx(Div, {})       // must be in scope

// children is an ordinary prop
<Card>{body}</Card>
<Card children={body} />           // identical

// An ELEMENT is a description; a COMPONENT is the function
const el = <Button />              // cheap object, nothing rendered
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Saved links
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        1↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        2↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        3↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • R02
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Think of it like a chef and a waiter. Render is the chef writing down the order — it can be rewritten, interrupted, or thrown in the bin, and nothing has happened yet. Commit is the waiter carrying the plate out — once that happens, it is real.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        So React may call your component function several times, or start and abandon it. Anything that changes the outside world (network calls, timers, writing to a global) must live in an effect or an event handler — never in the body of the component.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Side effect in the wrong phase
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        function Profile({ id }) {
  // WRONG - runs during render, may run twice, may be thrown away
  fetch(`/api/user/${id}`).then(...)

  // RIGHT - runs after commit, has cleanup
  useEffect(() => {
    let cancelled = false
    fetch(`/api/user/${id}`)
      .then(r => r.json())
      .then(d => { if (!cancelled) setUser(d) })
    return () => { cancelled = true }
  }, [id])
}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Saved links
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          1↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          2↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          3↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • R03
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Pre-18, updates inside a setTimeout, a promise callback, or a native listener each triggered their own render. React 18 made batching automatic in all of those places.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          If you genuinely need the DOM updated between two updates, flushSync opts out — but it costs a synchronous render, so it is for measuring, not for convenience.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Before and after 18
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          function handle() {
  setA(1); setB(2)        // 1 render in both 17 and 18
}

setTimeout(() => {
  setA(1); setB(2)        // React 17: TWO renders
}, 0)                     // React 18: ONE render

fetch(url).then(() => {
  setA(1); setB(2)        // same story
})

// Opt out when you must read the DOM in between
flushSync(() => setOpen(true))
inputRef.current.focus()  // the input now exists
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Saved links
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            1↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            2↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            3↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • R04
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            React does not diff cleverly across the whole tree — that would be too slow. It walks the tree in order and asks one question at each slot: is this the same type of thing as last time?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            If yes, it keeps the existing component and just updates the props. If no, it destroys the old one — including all its state and DOM — and mounts a fresh one. This is why conditionally swapping a component type resets everything inside it.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Same slot, different type = state is gone
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            // isEditing flips -> <input> is replaced, its state resets
{isEditing ? <input value={v}/> : <textarea value={v}/>}

// Defining a component INSIDE another is the classic version
function Parent() {
  // new function identity every render -> new type -> full remount
  const Child = () => <input />       // BUG: input loses focus + value
  return <Child />
}
// Fix: define Child outside Parent.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Saved links
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              1↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              2↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              3↗
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • R05
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Keys are how React matches items across renders. Without a stable key it falls back to position, which is fine for a static list and wrong for anything that can be reordered, filtered, or have items inserted at the top.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The bug is always the same shape: you delete the second item, and the third item inherits the second item checkbox, input value, or animation state — because as far as React knows, index 1 is still index 1.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The index-key bug
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              // BUG - delete an item and the NEXT row keeps the deleted row's input
{todos.map((todo, i) => <TodoRow key={i} todo={todo} />)}

// FIX - key by something stable and unique to the ITEM
{todos.map(todo => <TodoRow key={todo.id} todo={todo} />)}

// Keys only need to be unique among SIBLINGS, not globally.
// No stable id? Generate one when the item is created,
// not during render.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              My notes
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Saved links
